## What the plan proposes (the design under review)

### Trait extension (additive, non-breaking)

```rust
// In crates/ql-collab/src/transport.rs

pub trait Transport: Send {
    fn send(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), TransportError>;
    fn try_recv(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, TransportError>;
    fn flush_pending(&mut self) -> Result<(), TransportError> { Ok(()) }
    fn last_error(&self) -> Option<String> { None }

    /// V2.5 NEW: Returns a Send handle for draining queued sends
    /// WITHOUT holding any outer lock guarding the Transport itself.
    /// Default `None`. WebSocketTransport overrides.
    fn ack_handle(&self) -> Option<Box<dyn FlushAck + Send>> { None }
}

/// V2.5 NEW.
pub trait FlushAck: Send {
    fn wait_for_drain(&self) -> Result<(), TransportError>;
}
```

### WebSocketTransport implementation

```rust
// In crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs
pub struct WebSocketProgressAckHandle {
    queued_count: Arc<AtomicU64>,
    progress: Arc<(Mutex<u64>, Condvar)>,
    closed: Arc<AtomicBool>,
}

impl FlushAck for WebSocketProgressAckHandle {
    fn wait_for_drain(&self) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
        // EXACT same logic as WebSocketTransport::flush_pending
        // (currently at lib.rs:733-760), operating on Arc clones.
        if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            return Err(TransportError::Closed);
        }
        let target = self.queued_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
        let (counter_lock, cv) = &*self.progress;
        let mut counter = counter_lock.lock()
            .map_err(|e| TransportError::Io(format!("flush_pending lock poisoned: {e}")))?;
        while *counter < target {
            if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
                return Err(TransportError::Closed);
            }
            let (new_counter, _) = cv.wait_timeout(counter, Duration::from_millis(100))
                .map_err(|e| TransportError::Io(format!("flush_pending wait poisoned: {e}")))?;
            counter = new_counter;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Transport for WebSocketTransport {
    // ... existing unchanged ...
    fn ack_handle(&self) -> Option<Box<dyn FlushAck + Send>> {
        Some(Box::new(WebSocketProgressAckHandle {
            queued_count: Arc::clone(&self.queued_count),
            progress: Arc::clone(&self.progress),
            closed: Arc::clone(&self.closed),
        }))
    }
}
```

### napi binding refactor (THE CORE FIX)

```rust
// In crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs
// V2.4 current pattern (THE BUG):
#[napi(js_name = "flushPendingToTransport")]
pub async fn flush_pending_to_transport(&self) -> Result<()> {
    let inner = Arc::clone(&self.inner);
    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
        let mut guard = inner.lock();  // <-- HELD across the Condvar wait below
        guard.flush_pending_to_transport()  // <-- Condvar wait happens here
    }).await
        .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("flushPendingToTransport task: {e}")))?
        .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("{e}")))
}

// V2.5 proposed pattern:
#[napi(js_name = "flushPendingToTransport")]
pub async fn flush_pending_to_transport(&self) -> Result<()> {
    let handle_opt: Option<Box<dyn ql_collab::FlushAck + Send>> = {
        let inner = self.inner.lock();
        inner.flush_pending_handle()
    }; // <-- session lock RELEASED here
    let Some(handle) = handle_opt else { return Ok(()) };
    tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || handle.wait_for_drain())
        .await
        .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("flushPendingToTransport task: {e}")))?
        .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("{e}")))
}
```

### V2.6 BlockingTransport (test fixture)

```rust
// In crates/ql-collab/src/transport.rs (cfg-gated OR production — decision pending)
pub struct BlockingTransport {
    block_ms: u64,
    release: Arc<(Mutex<bool>, Condvar)>,
    // ... internal send/recv channels
}

impl Transport for BlockingTransport {
    fn send(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), TransportError> { /* enqueue locally */ }
    fn try_recv(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, TransportError> { /* drain */ }
    fn flush_pending(&mut self) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
        // Block for block_ms OR until release flag set, whichever comes first
    }
    fn ack_handle(&self) -> Option<Box<dyn FlushAck + Send>> {
        Some(Box::new(BlockingAckHandle { release: Arc::clone(&self.release), block_ms: self.block_ms }))
    }
}
```

JS-side exposed as `new engine.BlockingTransport(blockMs: number)` with a `release()` method, used for V2.5 contract tests.

### V2.5 contract test (mocha)

```ts
test('flushPendingToTransport does NOT block sync methods on the same session (V2.5)', async function () {
  this.timeout(5000);
  const session = createSession(1n);
  const t = new engine.BlockingTransport(500);  // blocks 500 ms
  session.attachTransport(t);
  session.appendPutValue(0, 0, 0, 1);
  session.flushDeltaToTransport();

  const flushP = session.flushPendingToTransport();
  // Under V2.4 binding pattern: opCount would block ~400-500 ms.
  // Under V2.5 binding pattern: opCount returns ~immediately.
  const start = Date.now();
  const count = session.opCount();
  const elapsed = Date.now() - start;
  assert.ok(elapsed < 100, `opCount during pending flush took ${elapsed}ms; expected < 100`);
  await flushP;
});
```

## The four specific questions Codex must answer

### Q1: Does the proposed refactor actually close V8-block?

Read V2.4 binding source (`crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:795-836`). Read V2.4 Opus audit HIGH-1 (`docs/audits/2026-05-22-phase-5-7-v2-4-opus.md:112-302`). Verify the lock-release pattern proposed in the plan above ACTUALLY drops the parking_lot Mutex before spawn_blocking takes ownership of the handle. Specifically:
- Does `let inner = self.inner.lock(); … inner.flush_pending_handle() }` release on the closing brace? (parking_lot Mutex: yes, on Drop.)
- Does `spawn_blocking(move || handle.wait_for_drain())` need to acquire the session mutex anywhere? (Plan says no — handle holds Arcs to progress directly.)
- Does the writer task hold the session mutex? (It does NOT — writer task is in WebSocketTransport, completely separate.)

### Q2: Is the chosen design (ack_handle returning Box) optimal?

Compare with alternatives:
- **Arc<dyn FlushAck>** instead of Box: avoids re-allocation if the same handle is reused but JS only calls flushPending once-per-session typically. Box is simpler.
- **async-trait** for ack_handle: would let the impl use `tokio::sync::Notify`, but would require an async-trait macro dep + the trait object becomes harder to send through spawn_blocking.
- **Opus's Option C** (try_lock + busy sentinel): breaking API change for read methods; documented as "probably not the V2.4 path" in Opus audit. Worse than Option A.
- **Notify-based Option B from V2.4 plan**: I rejected this as not solving the hazard — the wait is sync at the trait level, called from within spawn_blocking. Confirm rejection is correct.

### Q3: Is the BlockingTransport mocha contract test realistic?

- 500 ms block duration. 100 ms timing assertion. Margin: 400 ms.
- Mocha on CI: how flaky is the 100 ms threshold? Should we use 200 ms? Or measure RELATIVE (e.g., elapsed << block_duration * 0.5)?
- Should we add a deterministic synchronization point (release-on-signal) instead of timing-based?

### Q4: Production-cdylib vs feature-gated BlockingTransport

- API-surface concern: shipping `BlockingTransport` in production exposes it to malicious IDE extensions or curl-installed packages. But the only thing it can do is block its own session's flush_pending — no CRDT corruption.
- Build complexity: feature-gated requires `test-fixtures` feature on ql-collab + ql-bindings-node Cargo.toml; cdylib build script must enable it; mocha tests must work with the cdylib that has the feature on.
- Recommendation: which is the right trade-off?

## Other risks to scrutinize

5. **Race: flush_pending_handle extraction → detachTransport mid-wait**. The handle holds Arc clones of progress fields. If JS calls `detachTransport()` during the spawn_blocking wait, what happens?
   - WebSocketTransport's writer task is aborted on Drop (per `crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs::Drop`).
   - On writer abort, `closed = true` + `notify_all()`. The handle's wait_for_drain loops, sees `closed`, returns `Err(Closed)`.
   - BUT: the wait_timeout(100ms) means up to 100ms latency before observing closed. Acceptable?

6. **Box<dyn FlushAck + Send> overhead in spawn_blocking**. Each call allocates a Box. spawn_blocking submits the task to tokio's blocking pool — Box overhead is negligible compared to the cross-thread submission cost. Confirm.

7. **WebSocketProgressAckHandle Arc cloning soundness**. Three Arcs cloned from WebSocketTransport. After WebSocketTransport drops, the Arcs keep the underlying state alive — that's intentional? The writer task uses Arc clones too. After WebSocketTransport drops, the writer task is aborted but its Arc clones might still be alive briefly (during abort). Is there a race where wait_for_drain reads stale progress state?

8. **Does V2.5 refactor break existing engine workspace tests** (~4461 currently passing)? Specifically:
   - `crates/ql-collab/tests/auto_flush.rs` (which exercises flush behavior).
   - `crates/ql-collab/tests/websocket_transport.rs` (if any).
   - Loro CRDT tests in `crates/ql-collab/src/session.rs`.
   The Transport trait extension is non-breaking (default impl), so impact should be zero. Verify.

9. **`FlushAck: Send` vs `Send + Sync`**. The Box<dyn FlushAck + Send> is moved into spawn_blocking; never shared across threads after that. Send alone is sufficient. But there's a defensive argument for Send + Sync — would make it usable in patterns where the handle is cloned and shared. Trade-off?

     9	//! cdylib + napi-rs 3.x. The `#[napi]` derive macros generate the
    10	//! JS-facing class shape from the Rust struct. napi-rs handles:
    11	//!   - JS class lifecycle (`new`, finalize)
    12	//!   - `BigInt <-> u64` conversion for `PeerId`
    13	//!   - `Uint8Array <-> &[u8]`: `as_ref()` exposes a slice INTO the
    14	//!     JS-owned ArrayBuffer (verified via napi-rs 3.9.0
    15	//!     `arraybuffer.rs:653`'s `slice::from_raw_parts` on the SAB-or-AB
    16	//!     backing store). On export we hand ownership of a `Vec<u8>` to
    17	//!     JS via `Uint8Array::from`, which transfers the buffer rather
    18	//!     than copying.
    19	//!   - panic safety: **napi-rs 3.x does NOT wrap entry points in
    20	//!     `catch_unwind` by default** (Phase 5.7 V1 audit Codex H1 +
    21	//!     Opus H3, 2026-05-22 — verified by reading napi-derive-backend
    22	//!     5.0.4 `src/codegen/fn.rs:217-240`: the wrap is gated on
    23	//!     `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` opt-in). The V1 binding does NOT use
    24	//!     `catch_unwind` — instead, every `#[napi]` method
    25	//!     pre-validates inputs that could trigger engine-side `assert_*!`,
    26	//!     `panic!`, `unwrap`, or `expect`. Smoke caught one such hazard
    27	//!     (PeerId(0) → `CollabSession::new`'s `assert_ne!(peer, 0)` →
    28	//!     Node abort "failed to initiate panic, error 5"); the
    29	//!     `peer_id_from_bigint` helper now pre-rejects 0. V2+ each new
    30	//!     `#[napi]` method MUST sweep the engine for FFI-reachable
    31	//!     assertions and pre-validate the same way (see V2 backlog).
    32	//!
    33	//! ## V1 surface
    34	//!
    35	//! Single class `CollabSession` exposing the minimum methods that let
    36	//! TS code drive a round-trip:
    37	//!   - `new(peerId: bigint)`: wraps `ql_collab::CollabSession::new`
    38	//!   - static `fromSnapshot(peerId: bigint, bytes: Uint8Array)`:
    39	//!     wraps `from_snapshot`
    40	//!   - `appendPutValue(sheet, row, col, value)`: convenience for V1
    41	//!     (single Op variant; full Op enum binding deferred to V2)
    42	//!   - `exportBytes() -> Uint8Array`: snapshot
    43	//!   - `mergeBytes(bytes: Uint8Array) -> number`: returns merged op count
    44	//!   - `opCount() -> number`
    45	//!   - `pendingOpCount() -> number` (V2 V4 V1 step 2 helper)
    46	//!   - `hasPendingFlush() -> boolean` (V2 V3 step 3 helper)
    47	//!   - `peerId() -> bigint`
    48	//!
    49	//! ## V1 deferred (see `docs/phase5/5-7-v1-exit-packet.md`)
    50	//!
    51	//! Full V1-deferred-to-V2/V3 list lives in the V1 exit packet's
    52	//! "V1 deferred to V2" table. Summary: Transport binding
    53	//! (LoopbackTransport, WebSocketTransport, `attach_transport` /
    54	//! `detach_transport` / `has_transport` / `flush_to_transport` /
    55	//! `flush_delta_to_transport` / `flush_pending_to_transport` /
    56	//! `poll_remote` / `poll_remote_with_limit` /

    58	//! demo, undo/redo (UndoGroupGuard RAII translation), presence

    62	//! `.qbook` persistence import/export, `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` opt-in
    63	//! for defense in depth, SharedArrayBuffer defensive copy, BigInt
    64	//! return for `opCount`/`pendingOpCount`/`mergeBytes`,
    65	//! `mergeBytesDelta` companion, `@napi-rs/cli` publish pipeline,
    66	//! Windows-specific `.dll` naming, CI `QUANTBOOK_REQUIRE_ENGINE=1`

    70	//! ## Send + Sync
    71	//!
    72	//! **V2.4 (2026-05-22) UPDATE**: `CollabSession` is now `Send + Sync`
    73	//! (was `Send + !Sync` in V1+V2.1+V2.2+V2.3). The shape changed in V2.4
    74	//! from `inner: CoreCollabSession` to `inner: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<CoreCollabSession>>`
    75	//! as the closure for V2.3 audit's HIGH-1 (Rust UB via napi `&mut self`
    76	//! async re-entry). The Arc<Mutex> composition adds Sync via interior
    77	//! mutability — multiple shared `&CollabSession` references are sound;
    78	//! mutation flows through the Mutex.
    79	//!
    80	//! **Compile-asserted proof** (lib.rs near end of file): both Send AND
    81	//! Sync are pinned via `assert_send + assert_sync` const-fn pattern.
    82	//! Per Rule 4: positive proof is required (this is the V2.4
    83	//! re-pinning of what was V1's `!Sync` claim).
    84	//!
    85	//! **Underlying composition** (Send + Sync verified by source-walks):
    86	//!   - `CoreCollabSession: Send + !Sync` (engine claim at
    87	//!     `ql-collab/src/session.rs:87`, unchanged).
    88	//!   - `parking_lot::Mutex<T>: Send + Sync` when `T: Send`
    89	//!     (verified per `lock_api-0.4.14/src/mutex.rs:144`'s
    90	//!     `impl<R: RawMutex + Sync, T: Send> Sync for Mutex<R, T>`).
    91	//!   - `Arc<T>: Send + Sync` when `T: Send + Sync`.
    92	//!   - Therefore the V2.4 binding wrapper composition is `Send + Sync`.
    93	//!
    94	//! **V2.4 V8-block hazard (Opus V2.4 HIGH-1, NOT runtime-unsound)**:
    95	//! all napi methods on `CollabSession` acquire `self.inner.lock()`.
    96	//! While `flushPendingToTransport`'s spawn_blocking task holds the
    97	//! mutex during a Condvar wait (potentially seconds), JS sync method
    98	//! calls on the SAME session block the V8 event loop waiting for the
    99	//! lock. The IDE UI freezes for the wait duration. This is a UX
   100	//! hazard, not a soundness hazard. V2.5+ work plan documented at the
   101	//! `flushPendingToTransport` method below. The TS-side caller
   102	//! discipline today is: don't call other session methods while
   103	//! `flushPendingToTransport` is awaiting.

   132	/// **Phase 5.7 V1 megaudit closure (Codex HIGH, 2026-05-22):**
   133	/// Validate a JS Number argument that represents a u32-domain value.
   134	/// Rejects non-finite, negative, fractional, and out-of-u32 values
   135	/// with a distinct error message naming the calling method + parameter.
   136	///
   137	/// Why this exists: napi-rs's `napi_get_value_uint32` (used for `u32`
   138	/// params) applies ECMAScript `ToUint32`, silently coercing `-1` to
   139	/// `u32::MAX`, `NaN`/`Infinity` to `0`, fractions to floor-toward-zero.
   140	/// By taking the param as `f64` (raw `napi_get_value_double`) and
   141	/// validating here, we surface bad inputs as explicit JS Errors
   142	/// instead of corrupting workbook state.
   143	///
   144	/// **V2.2 audit closure (Codex LOW-1, 2026-05-22)**: added `method`
   145	/// context parameter so the error message names the actual calling
   146	/// method. Prior version hard-coded `"appendPutValue"` which produced
   147	/// confusing diagnostics when called from `pollRemoteWithLimit`.
   148	fn validate_u32_index(method: &str, name: &str, value: f64) -> Result<u32> {
   149	    if !value.is_finite() {
   150	        return Err(Error::from_reason(format!(
   151	            "{method}: {name} must be a finite non-negative integer, got {value}"
   152	        )));
   153	    }
   154	    if value < 0.0 {
   155	        return Err(Error::from_reason(format!(
   156	            "{method}: {name} must be a non-negative integer, got {value}"
   157	        )));
   158	    }
   159	    if value.fract() != 0.0 {
   160	        return Err(Error::from_reason(format!(
   161	            "{method}: {name} must be an integer, got {value}"
   162	        )));
   163	    }
   164	    if value > u32::MAX as f64 {
   165	        return Err(Error::from_reason(format!(
   166	            "{method}: {name} must be in [0, 4294967295] (u32::MAX), got {value}"
   167	        )));
   168	    }
   169	    Ok(value as u32)
   170	}

   172	/// Helper: convert a JS `BigInt` to `PeerId` with explicit rejection of
   173	/// FIVE failure modes:
   174	///   - negative BigInt (signed bit set) — PeerId is u64-domain
   175	///   - BigInt doesn't fit in u64 (lossless = false)
   176	///   - `peer_id == 0` — Loro's LEGACY_PEER sentinel; rejected with a
   177	///     PROACTIVE check here (the engine's `CollabSession::new` would
   178	///     hit `assert_ne!` and panic, which napi-rs 3.x doesn't reliably
   179	///     catch into a JS exception — observed during V1 smoke test:
   180	///     "failed to initiate panic, error 5, aborting"). Pre-validate
   181	///     in the FFI boundary to keep Node alive.
   182	///   - `peer_id == u64::MAX` — Loro's `PeerID::MAX` sentinel (verified
   183	///     via Loro 1.12 `loro-internal-1.12.0/src/loro.rs:184`:
   184	///     `if peer == PeerID::MAX { return Err(...) }`). Loro returns a
   185	///     CLEAN `Err` here (not a panic), so the FFI boundary is intact
   186	///     either way — but pre-rejecting at the binding gives a faster
   187	///     failure and a consistent error message paired with the
   188	///     `peer_id == 0` case.
   189	///
   190	/// napi-rs 3.x `BigInt::get_u64()` returns `(sign_bit: bool, value: u64,
   191	/// lossless: bool)`. `sign_bit == true` indicates a negative BigInt.
   192	/// Per CLAUDE.md no-fallback rule: each failure mode surfaces a distinct
   193	/// error message so IDE consumers can show the right user-facing copy.
   194	///
   195	/// **Phase 5.7 V1 smoke-test finding (2026-05-22)**: the original
   196	/// version of this helper allowed `peer_id == 0` through, expecting
   197	/// `CollabSession::new`'s `assert_ne!(0, 0)` to surface a clean error.
   198	/// In practice the panic ABORTED the Node process. Lesson:
   199	/// engine-level `assert_*!` is NOT a safe boundary for FFI. Every
   200	/// engine method that uses `assert_*!` for input validation needs a
   201	/// proactive pre-check at the FFI layer.
   202	///
   203	/// **Phase 5.7 V1 audit closure (Rule 4 / Opus boundary test,
   204	/// 2026-05-22)**: the closure test `BigInt boundary -- u64::MAX
   205	/// accepted, 2^64 rejected` revealed that Loro also reserves
   206	/// `PeerID::MAX` (in addition to 0). Added pre-rejection here for
   207	/// symmetry. V2 will sweep the engine + Loro for any other reserved
   208	/// sentinel values as the binding surface grows.
   209	fn peer_id_from_bigint(peer_id: &BigInt) -> Result<PeerId> {
   210	    let (sign_bit, peer_u64, lossless) = peer_id.get_u64();
   211	    if sign_bit {
   212	        return Err(Error::from_reason(
   213	            "peerId BigInt must be non-negative (PeerId is u64-domain)".to_string(),
   214	        ));
   215	    }
   216	    if !lossless {
   217	        return Err(Error::from_reason(
   218	            "peerId BigInt does not fit in u64 (lossy conversion)".to_string(),
   219	        ));
   220	    }

   778	    /// Async flush-pending — waits for the attached transport's writer
   779	    /// task to drain (level-1 local ack per V2 V4 V1 Tier K1 contract).
   780	    ///
   781	    /// Returns a JS `Promise<void>` that resolves when:
   782	    /// - the writer has completed `send` for every queued blob, OR
   783	    /// - the transport has been detached / dropped / errored.
   784	    ///
   785	    /// **V2.4 soundness** (closes V2.3 audit Codex+Opus HIGH-1+HIGH-2):
   786	    ///
   787	    /// - Takes `&self` (not `&mut self`). napi-rs codegen produces
   788	    ///   `&'static CollabSession` → multiple aliasing reads are sound
   789	    ///   by Rust's rules. No UB even under JS re-entry.
   790	    /// - `Arc::clone(&self.inner)` extracts a cloned reference to the
   791	    ///   inner `Arc<Mutex<CoreCollabSession>>`. The clone is moved into
   792	    ///   `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, which runs on a dedicated
   793	    ///   blocking thread (NOT a tokio worker). The Condvar wait
   794	    ///   doesn't occupy the napi-rs runtime's worker pool — closes
   795	    ///   V2.3 HIGH-2 (runtime starvation).
   796	    /// - Inside the blocking task, `inner.lock()` acquires the mutex.
   797	    ///   If a concurrent JS call holds the lock (e.g., another
   798	    ///   mid-flight method), this call blocks until the lock is
   799	    ///   available. No deadlock because mutex order is consistent
   800	    ///   (all session methods acquire the SAME mutex).
   801	    ///
   802	    /// **Failure modes**:
   803	    /// - No transport attached → returns `Ok(())` (NOT a rejection).
   804	    /// - Transport error during the wait → JS Error.
   805	    /// - The `spawn_blocking` task panics → JS Error.
   806	    ///
   807	    /// **V2.4 V8-block hazard (Opus V2.4 HIGH-1, 2026-05-22)** — known
   808	    /// trade-off, documented for caller discipline:
   809	    ///
   810	    /// While this method's `spawn_blocking` task holds `self.inner.lock()`
   811	    /// during a Condvar wait (the engine's `flush_pending_to_transport`
   812	    /// blocks on writer-progress; can be seconds for slow WS peers),
   813	    /// concurrent JS sync method calls on the SAME session block the
   814	    /// V8 event loop on lock acquisition. IDE UI freezes for the wait
   815	    /// duration.
   816	    ///
   817	    /// This is a UX hazard, NOT a soundness hazard (V2.3 audit's UB
   818	    /// hazard remains closed; V2.4 just trades it for a contention
   819	    /// hazard).
   820	    ///
   821	    /// **Caller discipline (today)**: don't call other `CollabSession`
   822	    /// methods on the same session while a `flushPendingToTransport`
   823	    /// promise is pending. Queue the calls behind the await.
   824	    ///
   825	    /// **V2.5+ engine refactor plan**: move the Condvar wait out of
   826	    /// `&mut self` exclusive access — either (a) clone an
   827	    /// `Arc<Transport>` inside the lock and release before waiting, or
   828	    /// (b) replace Condvar with `tokio::sync::Notify` so the wait
   829	    /// becomes truly async (no lock held). V2.5 will pick based on
   830	    /// the engine's writer-task lifecycle constraints.
   831	    #[napi(js_name = "flushPendingToTransport")]
   832	    pub async fn flush_pending_to_transport(&self) -> Result<()> {
   833	        let inner = Arc::clone(&self.inner);
   834	        tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
   835	            let mut guard = inner.lock();
   836	            guard.flush_pending_to_transport()
   837	        })
   838	        .await
   839	        .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("flushPendingToTransport task: {e}")))?
   840	        .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("{e}")))
   841	    }
   842	}

   133	# VS Code Copilot Instructions
   134	
   135	## Project Overview
   136	
   137	Visual Studio Code is built with a layered architecture using TypeScript, web APIs and Electron, combining web technologies with native app capabilities. The codebase is organized into key architectural layers:
   138	
   139	### Root Folders
   140	- `src/`: Main TypeScript source code with unit tests in `src/vs/*/test/` folders
   141	- `build/`: Build scripts and CI/CD tools
   142	- `extensions/`: Built-in extensions that ship with VS Code
   143	- `test/`: Integration tests and test infrastructure
   144	- `scripts/`: Development and build scripts
   145	- `resources/`: Static resources (icons, themes, etc.)
   146	- `out/`: Compiled JavaScript output (generated during build)
   147	
   148	### Core Architecture (`src/` folder)
   149	- `src/vs/base/` - Foundation utilities and cross-platform abstractions
   150	- `src/vs/platform/` - Platform services and dependency injection infrastructure
   151	- `src/vs/editor/` - Text editor implementation with language services, syntax highlighting, and editing features
   152	- `src/vs/workbench/` - Main application workbench for web and desktop
   153	  - `workbench/browser/` - Core workbench UI components (parts, layout, actions)
   154	  - `workbench/services/` - Service implementations
   155	  - `workbench/contrib/` - Feature contributions (git, debug, search, terminal, etc.)
   156	  - `workbench/api/` - Extension host and VS Code API implementation
   157	- `src/vs/code/` - Electron main process specific implementation
   158	- `src/vs/server/` - Server specific implementation
   159	
   160	The core architecture follows these principles:
   161	- **Layered architecture** - from `base`, `platform`, `editor`, to `workbench`
   162	- **Dependency injection** - Services are injected through constructor parameters
   163	- **Contribution model** - Features contribute to registries and extension points
   164	- **Cross-platform compatibility** - Abstractions separate platform-specific code
   165	
   166	### Built-in Extensions (`extensions/` folder)
   167	The `extensions/` directory contains first-party extensions that ship with VS Code:
   168	- **Language support** - `typescript-language-features/`, `html-language-features/`, `css-language-features/`, etc.
   169	- **Core features** - `git/`, `debug-auto-launch/`, `emmet/`, `markdown-language-features/`
   170	- **Themes** - `theme-*` folders for default color themes
   171	- **Development tools** - `extension-editing/`, `vscode-api-tests/`
   172	
   173	Each extension follows the standard VS Code extension structure with `package.json`, TypeScript sources, and contribution points to extend the workbench through the Extension API.
   174	
   175	### Finding Related Code
   176	1. **Semantic search first**: Use file search for general concepts
   177	2. **Grep for exact strings**: Use grep for error messages or specific function names
   178	3. **Follow imports**: Check what files import the problematic module
   179	4. **Check test files**: Often reveal usage patterns and expected behavior
   180	
   181	## Validating TypeScript changes
   182	
   183	MANDATORY: Always check the `VS Code - Build` watch task output via #runTasks/getTaskOutput for compilation errors before running ANY script or declaring work complete, then fix all compilation errors before moving forward.
   184	
   185	- NEVER run tests if there are compilation errors
   186	- NEVER use `npm run compile` to compile TypeScript files but call #runTasks/getTaskOutput instead
   187	
   188	### TypeScript compilation steps
   189	- Monitor the `VS Code - Build` task outputs for real-time compilation errors as you make changes
   190	- This task runs `Core - Build` and `Ext - Build` to incrementally compile VS Code TypeScript sources and built-in extensions
   191	- Start the task if it's not already running in the background
   192	
   193	### TypeScript validation steps
   194	- Use the run test tool if you need to run tests. If that tool is not available, then you can use `scripts/test.sh` (or `scripts\test.bat` on Windows) for unit tests (add `--grep <pattern>` to filter tests) or `scripts/test-integration.sh` (or `scripts\test-integration.bat` on Windows) for integration tests (integration tests end with .integrationTest.ts or are in /extensions/).
   195	- Use `npm run valid-layers-check` to check for layering issues

   220	pub enum AutoFlushPolicy {
   221	    /// Default. V2 V1 behavior preserved: caller drives flush + poll
   222	    /// explicitly via [`CollabSession::flush_to_transport`] +
   223	    /// [`CollabSession::poll_remote`]. Auto-flush never fires.

   225	    Disabled,

   227	    /// underlying `LoroDoc`. Triggers on: `append_op`, `merge_bytes`,
   228	    /// `update_presence`, `clear_presence`, `sweep_presence`,

   230	    ///
   231	    /// **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 1 (2026-05-21):** auto-flush routes

   233	    /// [`flush_to_transport`] (full-snapshot path). Wire payload is
   234	    /// O(per-op delta) instead of O(full state). The idempotency
   235	    /// short-circuit means a flush after no state change is a true
   236	    /// no-op (no transport.send invocation) — this closes the V2 V2
   237	    /// audit echo-loop class.
   238	    ///
   239	    /// **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 2 (2026-05-21):** `poll_remote*` now
   240	    /// triggers auto-flush AFTER the drain batch (one flush per
   241	    /// call, not per-blob) — bandwidth-efficient. Reverses the V2 V2
   242	    /// "receive-side excluded by design" exclusion now that V2 V3
   243	    /// step 1's idempotency guard prevents echo loops at the source
   244	    /// (Loro-deduped merge leaves VV unchanged → flush short-circuits
   245	    /// to `Ok(false)`). The 3-peer hub-fanout pattern now works
   246	    /// automatically.
   247	    ///
   248	    /// Does NOT trigger on:
   249	    /// - Accessor methods (read-only).
   250	    /// - Undo-group boundary methods (`start_undo_group` /
   251	    ///   `end_undo_group`) — only their inner appends fire, via
   252	    ///   `append_op`. Each mid-group append produces ONE auto-flush;
   253	    ///   the group is a LOCAL undo unit only (peers see each append
   254	    ///   land independently). Phase 5.5 V2 V2 audit closure (Opus
   255	    ///   L1) — undo-group atomicity-over-wire deferred to V2 V3.
   256	    /// - Transport-lifecycle methods (`attach_transport` etc.).
   257	    ///
   258	    /// If no transport is attached, this is silently a no-op (the
   259	    /// flush hook checks `self.transport.is_some()` first).
   260	    ///
   261	    /// **Partial-state contract on auto-flush error**: if the auto-
   262	    /// flush attempt fails (transport closed, I/O error), the
   263	    /// surrounding mutator (`append_op` etc.) returns
   264	    /// `Err(CollabSessionError::Transport(_))`. The local mutation
   265	    /// has ALREADY been committed to `self.log` (mutate-then-flush

   267	    /// limitation H7). Callers MUST treat their local state as
   268	    /// authoritative for the local UI and either retry the flush
   269	    /// (transport recovered) or detach the transport.
   270	    ///
   271	    /// **Symmetric-OnAppend (Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 1 closure,

   273	    /// transport is safe via the V2 V3 idempotency guard. The

     1	//! `ql-collab-ws` — WebSocket `Transport` impl for Phase 5
     2	//! collaboration.
     3	//!
     4	//! **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 4 (2026-05-21, this ship):** first
     5	//! production-grade [`Transport`](ql_collab::Transport) impl. Bridges
     6	//! tokio-tungstenite's async WebSocket client to the sync `Transport`
     7	//! trait via `tokio::sync::mpsc` channels and two spawned background
     8	//! tasks.
     9	//!
    10	//! ## Crate boundary rationale
    11	//!
    12	//! `ql-collab` core is purely sync and embeddable in non-tokio
    13	//! runtimes (e.g., an IDE main thread, future WASM target). Pulling
    14	//! tokio + tokio-tungstenite into the core would force that
    15	//! constraint on every consumer. Keeping the WebSocket impl in a
    16	//! separate crate means:
    17	//! - Consumers who only need `LoopbackTransport` (tests) or a custom
    18	//!   transport (in-process IPC, gRPC streaming) don't pay for tokio.
    19	//! - The async runtime lives at the application boundary, not in the
    20	//!   collaboration layer.
    21	//!
    22	//! ## Architecture
    23	//!
    24	//! ```text
    25	//!  caller (sync, e.g. inside CollabSession::append_op)
    26	//!    │
    27	//!    │  send(bytes)        try_recv() -> Option<bytes>
    28	//!    ▼                            ▲
    29	//!  WebSocketTransport             │
    30	//!    │ outbound_tx              inbound_rx
    31	//!    │  (mpsc::UnboundedSender)  (mpsc::UnboundedReceiver)
    32	//!    ▼                            ▲
    33	//!  writer_task (tokio)          reader_task (tokio)
    34	//!    │  awaits outbound_rx        │  awaits ws_stream.next()
    35	//!    ▼                            ▲
    36	//!    │  ws_sink.send(Binary)      │  inbound_tx.send(bytes)
    37	//!    ▼                            │
    38	//!  ===================== TCP socket =====================
    39	//! ```
    40	//!
    41	//! The two background tasks own the WebSocket halves
    42	//! (`SplitSink` + `SplitStream` via `futures_util::StreamExt::split`).
    43	//! `Drop` aborts both tasks (RAII close).
    44	//!
    45	//! ## V1 limitations (deferred to V2 V4)
    46	//!
    47	//! - **No TLS (`ws://` only).** Use a TLS-terminating reverse proxy
    48	//!   in front, or wait for V2 V4 `rustls` feature.
    49	//! - **No auto-reconnect.** Caller drives via `detach_transport` +
    50	//!   new `connect` + `attach_transport`. The Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 1
    51	//!   `last_flushed_vv = None` reset on attach delivers all accumulated
    52	//!   ops on reconnect (offline-write story).
    53	//! - **Unbounded outbound mpsc queue.** Memory growth is bounded in
    54	//!   practice for the common disconnect case: when the peer closes
    55	//!   the TCP socket, the reader task observes EOF / `Err` and sets
    56	//!   the closed flag; subsequent `send` calls fast-path to
    57	//!   `Err(Closed)` before reaching the unbounded mpsc. The genuine
    58	//!   growth window is the **dead-peer-but-not-closed** scenario
    59	//!   (server stops draining but doesn't tear down the TCP socket):
    60	//!   `ws_sink.send` stalls on TCP backpressure, `outbound_rx` grows
    61	//!   unboundedly, and the reader task may still be receiving heartbeat
    62	//!   frames so `closed` stays false. V2 V4 will switch to bounded
    63	//!   with caller-configurable backpressure policy (clarified in
    64	//!   V2 V3 step 4 audit closure, Opus M5).
    65	//! - **Client-only.** Server-side WebSocket impls use other libraries
    66	//!   (`axum-tungstenite`, `warp::ws`, etc.).
    67	//! - **Drops text/ping/pong/close frames as inbound data.** Loro
    68	//!   payloads are binary blobs; non-binary frames don't carry our
    69	//!   protocol. Close frames trigger reader task exit. Inbound Ping
    70	//!   frames: tokio-tungstenite queues a Pong response on the sink
    71	//!   for the next write — but with no app traffic the Pong is not
    72	//!   flushed until the next app send (clarified in V2 V3 step 4
    73	//!   audit closure, Opus L3). Server-side idle-timeout would then
    74	//!   close the connection. Text frames are silently dropped (a
    75	//!   future protocol extension could add a callback hook).
    76	//!
    77	//! ## Example
    78	//!
    79	//! ```ignore
    80	//! use ql_collab::{CollabSession, PeerId, AutoFlushPolicy};
    81	//! use ql_collab_ws::WebSocketTransport;
    82	//!
    83	//! let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?;
    84	//! let ws = rt.block_on(WebSocketTransport::connect("ws://localhost:8080"))?;
    85	//! let mut session = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1))?;
    86	//! session.attach_transport(ws);
    87	//! session.set_auto_flush_policy(AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend);
    88	//! // ... appends now propagate via WebSocket automatically ...
    89	//! ```
    90

    92	use std::sync::{Arc, Condvar, Mutex};
    93	use std::time::Duration;
    94	
    95	use futures_util::{SinkExt, StreamExt};
    96	use ql_collab::{Transport, TransportError};

   101	
   102	/// **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-B M2, 2026-05-21):**
   103	/// panic-safe task-exit guard. Held by the writer/reader tasks; its
   104	/// `Drop` impl runs even on panic-unwinding. If the task exits
   105	/// without calling [`Self::mark_clean_exit`], the guard treats it as
   106	/// an unexpected exit (panic) and sets `closed = true` + records a
   107	/// `RuntimeError` describing the panic.
   108	///
   109	/// Without this guard, a panic in `ws_sink.send`, `bytes.into()`, or
   110	/// any future inner code would leave the transport in `closed=false`
   111	/// with the task gone — callers would poll `try_recv` forever
   112	/// returning `Ok(None)` and `send` would queue bytes into an
   113	/// orphaned mpsc.
   114	struct TaskExitGuard {
   115	    task_name: &'static str,
   116	    closed: Arc<AtomicBool>,
   117	    last_error: Arc<Mutex<Option<WebSocketError>>>,
   118	    /// **V2 V4 V1 step 1 audit closure (Codex L1 / Opus M2, 2026-05-21):**
   119	    /// notify the `flush_pending` Condvar on panic exit so blocked
   120	    /// callers wake up immediately rather than waiting for the
   121	    /// `wait_timeout` tick. Same Arc as `WebSocketTransport::progress`.
   122	    progress: Arc<(Mutex<u64>, Condvar)>,
   123	    clean: bool,
   124	}
   125	
   126	impl TaskExitGuard {
   127	    fn new(
   128	        task_name: &'static str,
   129	        closed: Arc<AtomicBool>,
   130	        last_error: Arc<Mutex<Option<WebSocketError>>>,
   131	        progress: Arc<(Mutex<u64>, Condvar)>,
   132	    ) -> Self {
   133	        Self {
   134	            task_name,
   135	            closed,
   136	            last_error,
   137	            progress,
   138	            clean: false,
   139	        }
   140	    }
   141	
   142	    /// Call before the task body exits via any normal path
   143	    /// (Err arm, stream-end, clean recv-None). Skipping this
   144	    /// is the signal that the task panicked.
   145	    fn mark_clean_exit(mut self) {
   146	        self.clean = true;
   147	    }
   148	}
   149	
   150	impl Drop for TaskExitGuard {
   151	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   152	        if !self.clean {
   153	            // Panic path: stash the panic signal in last_error
   154	            // BEFORE setting closed (so a concurrent reader sees
   155	            // the error first). Per CLAUDE.md no-fallback rule,
   156	            // surface the panic loudly rather than swallowing.
   157	            record_runtime_error(
   158	                &self.last_error,
   159	                format!("ql-collab-ws {} task panicked", self.task_name),
   160	            );
   161	            self.closed.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   162	            // V2 V4 V1 step 1 audit closure (Opus M2): wake any
   163	            // flush_pending waiter so they observe the closed flag
   164	            // without a 100ms timeout delay.
   165	            self.progress.1.notify_all();
   166	        }
   167	    }
   168	}
   169	
   170	/// **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-B M3, 2026-05-21):** surface
   171	/// poisoned-mutex condition as a `RuntimeError` rather than the
   172	/// previous `.lock().ok()` swallow. A poisoned mutex means a holder
   173	/// panicked while populating the slot — the caller deserves to know
   174	/// the slot's most-recent error was lost.
   175	fn record_runtime_error(slot: &Arc<Mutex<Option<WebSocketError>>>, message: String) {
   176	    match slot.lock() {
   177	        Ok(mut guard) => {
   178	            *guard = Some(WebSocketError::RuntimeError(message));
   179	        }
   180	        Err(poisoned) => {
   181	            // Recover the inner mutex despite poison; overwrite with
   182	            // a message that explicitly notes the poisoning so the
   183	            // caller can detect a prior panic-during-error-stash.
   184	            let mut guard = poisoned.into_inner();
   185	            *guard = Some(WebSocketError::RuntimeError(format!(
   186	                "{message} (note: error slot mutex was poisoned by prior panic)"
   187	            )));
   188	        }
   189	    }
   190	}

   192	/// Errors emitted by [`WebSocketTransport`].
   193	///
   194	/// Distinguishes connect-time errors (`InvalidUrl`, `ConnectFailed`,
   195	/// `HandshakeFailed`) from runtime errors observed by the background
   196	/// reader/writer tasks (`RuntimeError`). Connect-time errors surface
   197	/// as the `Result::Err` from [`WebSocketTransport::connect`]; runtime
   198	/// errors are stashed on the transport and readable via
   199	/// [`WebSocketTransport::last_error`] AFTER the trait `send`/`try_recv`
   200	/// surface `TransportError::Closed`.
   201	///
   202	/// Maps tungstenite errors opaquely — we don't want to leak
   203	/// tungstenite types into the public API.
   204	///
   205	/// **V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1, 2026-05-21):** the prior
   206	/// ship discarded background-task errors (`if let Err(_e)`), flattening
   207	/// 8 distinct tungstenite::Error variants into a uniform `Closed` at
   208	/// the trait boundary. This violated the CLAUDE.md no-fallbacks rule
   209	/// (errors must be visible) and made it impossible for IDE consumers
   210	/// driving reconnect handshakes to distinguish "connection lost" from
   211	/// "auth failed". Adds `RuntimeError(String)` variant + `last_error()`
   212	/// accessor; both tasks now populate the shared `last_error` slot on
   213	/// non-graceful exit.
   214	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Error)]
   215	#[non_exhaustive]
   216	pub enum WebSocketError {
   217	    /// The URL string failed to parse or is missing required parts.
   218	    /// Per CLAUDE.md no-fallback rule: surface clearly, don't silently
   219	    /// retry with a "fixed up" URL.
   220	    #[error("invalid WebSocket URL: {0}")]
   220	    #[error("invalid WebSocket URL: {0}")]
   221	    InvalidUrl(String),
   222	
   223	    /// TCP connect failed (refused, timeout, DNS, etc.).
   224	    #[error("WebSocket connection failed: {0}")]
   225	    ConnectFailed(String),
   226	
   227	    /// WebSocket protocol handshake failed (HTTP upgrade rejected,
   228	    /// invalid response, etc.).
   229	    #[error("WebSocket handshake failed: {0}")]
   230	    HandshakeFailed(String),
   231	
   232	    /// Background reader/writer task observed a runtime failure
   233	    /// (peer reset, IO error, protocol violation, capacity exceeded,
   234	    /// etc.) AFTER a successful connect. Surfaces via
   235	    /// [`WebSocketTransport::last_error`] once the trait-level
   236	    /// `Closed` has been observed.
   237	    #[error("WebSocket runtime error: {0}")]
   238	    RuntimeError(String),
   239	}

   241	/// Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 4 — WebSocket `Transport` impl.
   242	///
   243	/// Bridges async tokio-tungstenite to the sync `Transport` trait via
   244	/// `tokio::sync::mpsc` channels and two spawned background tasks.
   245	/// See module-level docs for architecture diagram.
   246	///
   247	/// ## Construction
   248	///
   249	/// Use [`connect`](Self::connect) — async fn that performs the WS
   250	/// handshake. Caller pattern from sync code:
   251	///
   252	/// ```ignore
   253	/// let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?;
   254	/// let ws = rt.block_on(WebSocketTransport::connect("ws://host:port"))?;
   255	/// session.attach_transport(ws);
   256	/// ```
   257	///
   258	/// ## Send + Sync
   259	///
   260	/// `WebSocketTransport: Send + Sync` (Send pinned by the V2 V3
   261	/// step 4 manual `const _ASSERT_WEBSOCKET_TRANSPORT_SEND`, Sync
   262	/// pinned by V2 V4 V1 step 3 `static_assertions::assert_impl_all!` —
   263	/// both compile-time checks at the end of this file). Note: the
   264	/// prior
   265	/// V2 V3 step 4 docstring (and Tier J3 backlog entry) incorrectly
   266	/// claimed `!Sync` based on the intuition that the single-consumer
   267	/// mpsc receiver should prevent sharing. In Rust, `Sync` means "`&T`
   268	/// can be sent across threads" — orthogonal to "`&mut T` access is
   269	/// exclusive." `try_recv` takes `&mut self`, so concurrent receives
   270	/// are already prevented by the borrow checker. All fields
   271	/// (mpsc handles, `Arc<AtomicBool>`, `Arc<Mutex<_>>`, `JoinHandle`)
   272	/// are `Send + Sync`, making the composite `Send + Sync`.
   273	///
   274	/// **Why this matters**: matches the `CollabSession::transport:
   275	/// Box<dyn Transport + Send>` constraint (only `Send` is required at
   276	/// the trait boundary; `Sync` is a bonus that allows future
   277	/// `Arc<WebSocketTransport>` wrappers if a consumer needs them).
   278	/// **Tier J3 closure (V2 V4 V1 step 3, 2026-05-21):** corrected the
   279	/// docstring + the backlog entry; pinned BOTH bounds with positive
   280	/// compile-time asserts.
   281	pub struct WebSocketTransport {
   282	    /// Caller-side sender feeding the writer task. Sync write via
   283	    /// `UnboundedSender::send` (which is non-blocking).
   284	    outbound_tx: mpsc::UnboundedSender<Vec<u8>>,
   285	    /// Caller-side receiver pulling from the reader task. Sync drain
   286	    /// via `UnboundedReceiver::try_recv`.
   287	    inbound_rx: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<Vec<u8>>,
   288	    /// Set true when either task observes a permanent failure (WS
   289	    /// close, IO error, peer disconnect) OR caller invokes
   290	    /// [`close`](Self::close). Both `send` and `try_recv` honor this
   291	    /// flag per the `Transport` trait drain-before-close contract.
   292	    closed: Arc<AtomicBool>,
   293	    /// **V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1, 2026-05-21):** stash
   294	    /// the most recent task-observed runtime error so callers can
   295	    /// distinguish "peer reset" from "auth rejected" from "capacity
   296	    /// exceeded" etc. Populated by the writer task on `ws_sink.send`
   297	    /// error and the reader task on stream `Err`. Stays `None` for
   298	    /// clean shutdowns (caller `close()`, Drop, or graceful Close
   299	    /// frame from peer).
   300	    last_error: Arc<Mutex<Option<WebSocketError>>>,
   301	    /// **Phase 5.5 V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   302	    /// Incremented by [`Transport::send`] on Ok return. Total bytes
   303	    /// queued lifetime (monotonic, never resets). Compared against
   304	    /// [`Self::progress.0`] in [`Transport::flush_pending`] to detect
   305	    /// when the writer task has caught up.
   306	    queued_count: Arc<AtomicU64>,
   307	    /// **Phase 5.5 V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   308	    /// `(counter, condvar)` pair. Counter is incremented by the writer
   309	    /// task AFTER each successful `ws_sink.send`. Condvar is notified
   310	    /// on each counter increment AND on `closed`-flag transition (so
   311	    /// `flush_pending` callers waiting on the Condvar wake up and
   312	    /// observe the closed state). Sync primitives (not tokio) because
   313	    /// `flush_pending` is called from sync caller code and needs to
   314	    /// block synchronously without a tokio runtime context.
   315	    progress: Arc<(Mutex<u64>, Condvar)>,
   316	    /// Background tokio task that drains `outbound_rx` and writes
   317	    /// `Message::Binary` frames to the WebSocket sink. Aborted on
   318	    /// `Drop`.
   319	    writer_task: JoinHandle<()>,
   320	    /// Background tokio task that polls the WebSocket stream and
   321	    /// pushes binary payloads into `inbound_tx`. Aborted on `Drop`.
   322	    reader_task: JoinHandle<()>,
   323	}
   324	
   325	impl std::fmt::Debug for WebSocketTransport {
   326	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
   327	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 4 (Tier K6, 2026-05-21):** surface
   328	        // last_error presence in Debug output. When a transport is
   329	        // closed and both tasks have exited, knowing whether the
   330	        // error slot is populated matters more than knowing the
   331	        // booleans alone — it distinguishes "clean caller-close"
   332	        // (last_error=None) from "task observed a runtime failure"
   333	        // (last_error=Some). Per V2 V3 step 5 megaudit Opus-B L2.
   334	        f.debug_struct("WebSocketTransport")
   335	            .field("closed", &self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
   336	            .field("writer_finished", &self.writer_task.is_finished())
   337	            .field("reader_finished", &self.reader_task.is_finished())
   338	            .field("last_error_present", &self.last_error().is_some())
   339	            .finish()
   340	    }
   341	}
   342	
   343	impl WebSocketTransport {
   344	    /// Connect to a WebSocket server at `url` (e.g. `ws://host:port/path`).
   345	    ///
   346	    /// Must be called from within a tokio runtime context (the two
   347	    /// background tasks are spawned via `tokio::spawn`). The typical
   348	    /// pattern from sync code is `runtime.block_on(connect(...))`.
   349	    ///
   350	    /// On success, returns a fully-wired transport: send/recv channels
   351	    /// connected, background tasks running. On failure, returns one
   352	    /// of the [`WebSocketError`] variants with the underlying cause.
   353	    pub async fn connect(url: &str) -> Result<Self, WebSocketError> {
   354	        // tokio-tungstenite::connect_async handles URL parse + TCP
   355	        // connect + WS handshake in one call. Distinguish the failure
   356	        // modes via the returned error string match — opaque to keep
   357	        // tungstenite types out of our public API.
   358	        let (ws_stream, _response) = tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(url).await.map_err(|e| {
   359	            let msg = e.to_string();
   360	            // Coarse classification — tungstenite::Error doesn't have a
   361	            // clean discriminant for "URL parse" vs "TCP connect" vs
   362	            // "handshake". Use the error type to route.
   363	            match e {
   364	                tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Error::Url(_) => WebSocketError::InvalidUrl(msg),
   365	                tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Error::Io(_) => WebSocketError::ConnectFailed(msg),
   366	                tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Error::Http(_)
   367	                | tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::Error::HttpFormat(_) => {
   368	                    WebSocketError::HandshakeFailed(msg)
   369	                }
   370	                _ => WebSocketError::HandshakeFailed(msg),
   371	            }
   372	        })?;
   373	
   374	        let (mut ws_sink, mut ws_stream) = ws_stream.split();
   375	
   376	        let (outbound_tx, mut outbound_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<Vec<u8>>();
   377	        let (inbound_tx, inbound_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel::<Vec<u8>>();
   378	
   379	        let closed = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
   380	        let closed_writer = Arc::clone(&closed);
   381	        let closed_reader = Arc::clone(&closed);
   382	        let last_error = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None::<WebSocketError>));
   383	        let last_error_writer = Arc::clone(&last_error);
   384	        let last_error_reader = Arc::clone(&last_error);
   385	
   386	        // **Phase 5.5 V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   387	        // Track writer-task progress for `Transport::flush_pending`.
   388	        // `queued_count` is incremented by `send()` after a successful
   389	        // mpsc enqueue. `progress.0` is the counter of bytes
   390	        // successfully flushed to the WebSocket sink, incremented by
   391	        // the writer task. `progress.1` (Condvar) is notified after
   392	        // each progress increment AND on closed-flag transitions, so
   393	        // `flush_pending` blocked in `wait_timeout` can wake and
   394	        // observe the new state.
   395	        let queued_count = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
   396	        let progress = Arc::new((Mutex::new(0u64), Condvar::new()));
   397	        let progress_writer = Arc::clone(&progress);
   398	        let progress_reader = Arc::clone(&progress);
   399	
   400	        // Writer task: drains outbound mpsc, writes Binary frames to
   401	        // the WS sink. Exits on outbound_rx close (caller dropped
   402	        // outbound_tx, which happens when WebSocketTransport drops)
   403	        // OR on sink error.
   404	        //
   405	        // **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-B M2, 2026-05-21):**
   406	        // wrap the body in a TaskExitGuard so panic-unwinding
   407	        // sets `closed = true` + records a Panic error. Without
   408	        // this, a panic in `ws_sink.send`/`bytes.into()` leaves the
   409	        // transport in `closed=false` state with the writer task
   410	        // gone — callers send-loop forever returning Ok-but-discarded
   411	        // bytes.
   412	        let writer_task = tokio::spawn(async move {
   413	            let _guard = TaskExitGuard::new(
   414	                "writer",
   415	                Arc::clone(&closed_writer),
   416	                Arc::clone(&last_error_writer),
   417	                Arc::clone(&progress_writer),
   418	            );
   419	            while let Some(bytes) = outbound_rx.recv().await {
   420	                if let Err(e) = ws_sink.send(Message::Binary(bytes.into())).await {
   421	                    // V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1): stash the
   422	                    // tungstenite error string so callers can read it
   423	                    // via last_error() after seeing TransportError::Closed.
   424	                    record_runtime_error(&last_error_writer, e.to_string());
   425	                    closed_writer.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   426	                    // V2 V4 V1 step 1: wake any flush_pending waiters
   427	                    // so they observe the now-set closed flag.
   428	                    progress_writer.1.notify_all();
   429	                    _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   430	                    return;
   431	                }
   432	                // V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1): writer task successfully
   433	                // wrote one byte blob to the WS sink. Advance the
   434	                // progress counter + notify any flush_pending waiters.
   435	                // **Step 1 audit closure (Opus L1):** poisoned-mutex
   436	                // handling — recover via PoisonError::into_inner()
   437	                // so a prior panic doesn't permanently freeze the
   438	                // counter at a stale value. Symmetric with
   439	                // last_error mutex handling.
   440	                let mut counter = match progress_writer.0.lock() {
   441	                    Ok(g) => g,
   442	                    Err(poisoned) => poisoned.into_inner(),
   443	                };
   444	                *counter += 1;
   445	                progress_writer.1.notify_all();
   446	            }
   447	            // outbound_rx closed (sender dropped) — clean shutdown.
   448	            // Attempt a graceful WS close frame; ignore errors (peer
   449	            // may already be gone). NOTE: under Drop, abort() runs
   450	            // before outbound_tx drops in field-decl order, so this
   451	            // arm is unreachable from Drop — see M2 closure note on
   452	            // the Drop impl. Reachable from a future "soft close" API
   453	            // that detaches outbound_tx explicitly.
   454	            let _ = ws_sink.close().await;
   455	            // V2 V4 V1 step 1: wake any flush_pending waiters on
   456	            // clean exit too (graceful "soft close" path).
   457	            progress_writer.1.notify_all();
   458	            _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   459	        });
   460	
   460	
   461	        // Reader task: polls WS stream; pushes binary payloads into
   462	        // inbound mpsc. Exits on stream end, error, or Close frame.
   463	        //
   464	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 audit closure (Codex L1 / Opus M1):** every
   465	        // closed-flag transition from the reader task now also calls
   466	        // `progress.1.notify_all()` so flush_pending waiters wake up
   467	        // immediately, not after a 100ms timeout. The TaskExitGuard
   468	        // also notifies on panic path via its Drop impl.
   469	        let reader_task = tokio::spawn(async move {
   470	            let _guard = TaskExitGuard::new(
   471	                "reader",
   472	                Arc::clone(&closed_reader),
   473	                Arc::clone(&last_error_reader),
   474	                Arc::clone(&progress_reader),
   475	            );
   476	            while let Some(msg_result) = ws_stream.next().await {
   477	                match msg_result {
   478	                    Ok(Message::Binary(bytes)) => {
   479	                        if inbound_tx.send(bytes.to_vec()).is_err() {
   480	                            // Receiver dropped (WebSocketTransport
   481	                            // dropped) — exit cleanly. Set closed
   482	                            // for state-machine symmetry (Opus-B L1).
   483	                            closed_reader.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   484	                            progress_reader.1.notify_all();
   485	                            _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   486	                            return;
   487	                        }
   488	                    }
   489	                    Ok(Message::Close(frame)) => {
   490	                        // **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-B M4
   491	                        // + Codex L2, 2026-05-21):** capture the
   492	                        // close-frame code+reason if present. Empty
   493	                        // / missing CloseFrame stays last_error=None
   494	                        // for graceful close; populated CloseFrame
   495	                        // surfaces the application-level signal
   496	                        // (e.g., "session expired, please reauth").
   497	                        if let Some(cf) = frame {
   498	                            if !cf.reason.is_empty() || u16::from(cf.code) != 1000 {
   499	                                record_runtime_error(
   500	                                    &last_error_reader,
   501	                                    format!(
   502	                                        "peer close frame: code={}, reason={}",
   503	                                        u16::from(cf.code),
   504	                                        cf.reason
   505	                                    ),
   506	                                );
   507	                            }
   508	                        }
   509	                        closed_reader.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   510	                        progress_reader.1.notify_all();
   511	                        _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   512	                        return;
   513	                    }
   514	                    Ok(
   515	                        Message::Text(_) | Message::Ping(_) | Message::Pong(_) | Message::Frame(_),
   516	                    ) => {
   517	                        // Non-binary frames dropped per protocol
   518	                        // contract (see module-level V1 limits).
   519	                    }
   520	                    Err(e) => {
   521	                        // V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1): stash
   522	                        // the tungstenite error so callers can
   523	                        // distinguish runtime causes via last_error().
   524	                        record_runtime_error(&last_error_reader, e.to_string());
   525	                        closed_reader.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   526	                        progress_reader.1.notify_all();
   527	                        _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   528	                        return;
   529	                    }
   530	                }
   531	            }
   532	            // **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Codex L2 + Opus-B M4,
   533	            // 2026-05-21):** stream ended without a Close frame.
   534	            // Distinguishable from clean caller-close (last_error
   535	            // stays None) and from explicit Close frame (last_error
   536	            // populated above if frame had reason or non-1000 code).
   537	            record_runtime_error(
   538	                &last_error_reader,
   539	                "peer stream ended without close frame".to_string(),
   540	            );
   541	            closed_reader.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   542	            progress_reader.1.notify_all();
   543	            _guard.mark_clean_exit();
   544	        });
   545	
   546	        Ok(Self {
   547	            outbound_tx,
   548	            inbound_rx,
   549	            closed,
   550	            last_error,
   551	            queued_count,
   552	            progress,
   553	            writer_task,
   554	            reader_task,
   555	        })
   556	    }
   557	
   558	    /// True if this transport has been closed — either explicitly via
   559	    /// [`close`](Self::close), via Drop, or by either background task
   560	    /// observing a permanent failure (peer disconnect, WS Close frame,
   561	    /// IO error).
   562	    pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool {
   563	        self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
   564	    }
   565	
   566	    /// **V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1, 2026-05-21):** read the
   567	    /// most recent task-observed runtime error, if any. Returns `None`
   568	    /// for clean shutdowns (caller [`close`](Self::close), Drop, or
   569	    /// graceful Close frame from peer); returns `Some(RuntimeError(_))`
   570	    /// when the writer's `ws_sink.send` or the reader's `ws_stream.next`
   571	    /// surfaced an error before exiting.
   572	    ///
   573	    /// Read AFTER observing [`TransportError::Closed`] from
   574	    /// [`Transport::send`] or [`Transport::try_recv`] to distinguish
   575	    /// "peer reset" vs "auth rejected" vs "capacity exceeded" etc.
   576	    /// IDE consumers driving reconnect handshakes use this to choose
   577	    /// the right user-facing message and backoff strategy.
   578	    ///
   579	    /// Returns a clone (cheap — `WebSocketError` is small + `Clone`).
   580	    ///
   581	    /// **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-B M3, 2026-05-21):**
   582	    /// poisoned mutex no longer silently returns `None`. Recovers
   583	    /// the inner via `PoisonError::into_inner()` so the slot's
   584	    /// most-recent contents stay readable across the poison boundary.
   585	    pub fn last_error(&self) -> Option<WebSocketError> {
   586	        match self.last_error.lock() {
   587	            Ok(guard) => guard.clone(),
   588	            Err(poisoned) => poisoned.into_inner().clone(),
   589	        }
   590	    }
   591	
   592	    /// Explicitly mark this transport closed. Subsequent
   593	    /// [`Transport::send`] calls return `Err(Closed)`; subsequent
   594	    /// [`Transport::try_recv`] calls drain the inbound queue first,
   595	    /// then return `Err(Closed)` (per trait contract).
   596	    ///
   597	    /// Does NOT abort the background tasks — only Drop does that. If
   598	    /// the caller wants the tasks gone, drop the transport.
   599	    ///
   600	    /// **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** also notifies the
   601	    /// flush_pending Condvar so any concurrent `flush_pending` waiter
   602	    /// wakes up and observes the new closed state.
   603	    pub fn close(&self) {
   604	        self.closed.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   605	        self.progress.1.notify_all();
   606	    }
   607	}
   608	
   609	impl Drop for WebSocketTransport {
   610	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   611	        // **V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M2, 2026-05-21):** the
   612	        // sole shutdown path under current design is `abort()` on both
   613	        // task handles. The graceful `outbound_rx.recv() -> None ->
   614	        // ws_sink.close()` branch in the writer task is UNREACHABLE
   615	        // FROM DROP because `Drop::drop` runs before the struct's
   616	        // fields drop (Rust drop order: body first, then fields in
   617	        // decl order). So `outbound_tx` is still alive when we call
   618	        // `writer_task.abort()`. The graceful arm only fires if a
   619	        // future "soft close" API explicitly detaches `outbound_tx`
   620	        // before drop — not part of the current MVP.
   621	        //
   622	        // `closed = true` ordering: set first so any concurrent
   623	        // sync `send`/`try_recv` observes Closed via the flag check
   624	        // before the task abort propagates.
   625	        //
   626	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** also notify the
   627	        // flush_pending Condvar — a caller awaiting a long-running
   628	        // flush would otherwise wait until the next wait_timeout
   629	        // tick to observe the closed flag. (Unreachable in practice
   630	        // because Drop is called on a unique `&mut self` so no
   631	        // concurrent flush_pending can be in flight, but kept for
   632	        // safety + future shared-reference APIs.)
   633	        self.closed.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   634	        self.progress.1.notify_all();
   635	        self.writer_task.abort();
   636	        self.reader_task.abort();
   637	    }
   638	}
   639	
   640	impl Transport for WebSocketTransport {
   641	    fn send(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
   642	        // **LOAD-BEARING** (V2 V3 step 4 audit closure, Opus M4): this
   643	        // closed-flag check MUST precede `outbound_tx.send`. The
   644	        // `collab_session_websocket_send_after_close_surfaces_closed`
   645	        // integration test depends on observing `Closed` here (the
   646	        // reader task sets `closed = true` on peer disconnect; the
   647	        // writer task may still be parked on `outbound_rx.recv` and
   648	        // hasn't yet seen the broken sink). If a future refactor
   649	        // reorders this check (e.g., to enable an outbox-queuing-
   650	        // while-closed feature), that test will flake.
   651	        if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   652	            return Err(TransportError::Closed);
   653	        }
   654	        // UnboundedSender::send returns Err iff the receiver dropped.
   655	        // The receiver lives in the writer task; if it dropped, the
   656	        // task exited (panic, abort, or graceful). Treat as Closed.
   657	        self.outbound_tx
   658	            .send(bytes.to_vec())
   659	            .map_err(|_| TransportError::Closed)?;
   660	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   661	        // Bump the queued-count counter AFTER successful mpsc enqueue.
   662	        // flush_pending() reads this as the target the writer task
   663	        // must catch up to.
   664	        self.queued_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
   665	        Ok(())
   666	    }
   667	
   668	    fn try_recv(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, TransportError> {
   669	        // Drain-before-close per `Transport` trait contract
   670	        // (transport.rs:112-115): "Closed only when channel
   671	        // permanently closed AND internal queue is empty."
   672	        use mpsc::error::TryRecvError;
   673	        match self.inbound_rx.try_recv() {
   674	            Ok(bytes) => Ok(Some(bytes)),
   675	            Err(TryRecvError::Empty) => {
   676	                if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   677	                    Err(TransportError::Closed)
   678	                } else {
   679	                    Ok(None)
   680	                }
   681	            }
   682	            Err(TryRecvError::Disconnected) => {
   683	                // Reader task exited and dropped inbound_tx. Mark
   684	                // closed so subsequent calls fast-path; treat as
   685	                // Closed for this call (the queue is empty AND the
   686	                // upstream is permanently gone).
   687	                self.closed.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   688	                Err(TransportError::Closed)
   689	            }
   690	        }
   691	    }
   692	
   693	    /// **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-A H1, 2026-05-21):**
   694	    /// override the default `None` to expose the runtime-error cause
   695	    /// through the trait so [`ql_collab::CollabSession::transport_last_error`]
   696	    /// can reach it after `attach_transport` consumes the concrete
   697	    /// type into `Box<dyn Transport + Send>`.
   698	    ///
   699	    /// Returns the underlying [`WebSocketError`]'s `Display` string.
   700	    /// Consumers wanting to discriminate handshake/connect/runtime
   700	    /// Consumers wanting to discriminate handshake/connect/runtime
   701	    /// reasons can pattern-match on substrings or use the prefix
   702	    /// (`"WebSocket runtime error: ..."`) to detect the variant —
   703	    /// for stronger typing keep a parallel reference to the concrete
   704	    /// transport before attach.
   705	    fn last_error(&self) -> Option<String> {
   706	        Self::last_error(self).map(|e| e.to_string())
   707	    }

   709	    /// **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**

   974	    /// **Phase 5.5 V2 V4 V1 step 2 (2026-05-21) — Tier I1.** Count of
   975	    /// Loro causal-history entries (per-peer counter deltas) added to
   976	    /// the local op log since the last successful flush to the

   980	    /// difference rather than just a boolean).
   981	    ///
   982	    /// # Implementation
   983	    ///
   984	    /// Computed by VV math: for each peer in `current_vv`, take the
   985	    /// per-peer counter delta from the corresponding entry in
   986	    /// `last_flushed_vv` (or 0 if absent), and sum the positive
   987	    /// deltas. VV counters are monotonic per peer in Loro's causal
   988	    /// history — they only INCREASE within a single peer's lifetime
   989	    /// (each new op the peer authors gets the next counter value).
   990	    /// This makes the VV-based count strictly monotonic under all
   991	    /// existing log mutations including `undo` (which Loro records as
   992	    /// a new causal-history entry that advances the VV even though it
   993	    /// retracts a visible op from the LoroList).
   994	    ///
   995	    /// **V2 V4 V1 step 2 audit closure (Codex M1 / Opus H1,
   996	    /// 2026-05-21):** the initial ship used `self.log.len()` (visible
   997	    /// LoroList length) as the count source. That's NOT monotonic
   998	    /// under undo — Loro's `UndoManager` retracts ops from the visible
   999	    /// list, so `log.len()` can shrink while `current_vv` still
  1000	    /// advances. Result: `pending_op_count() == 0` while
  1001	    /// `has_pending_flush() == true` — divergent observability that
  1002	    /// breaks the documented sibling relationship. The convergent
  1003	    /// audit finding caught this; the closure switched to VV math,
  1004	    /// which is monotonic under undo (the undo's inverse op is a new
  1005	    /// VV entry).
  1006	    ///
  1007	    /// # IDE consumer use cases
  1008	    ///
  1009	    /// - **Bounded-queue policy**: "if `pending_op_count() > 1000`,
  1010	    ///   switch the editor to read-only mode until reconnect."
  1011	    /// - **Status indicator gradient**: "🟢 Synced if 0, 🟡 N pending
  1012	    ///   if 1..50, 🟠 backlog warning if >50."

  1014	    ///   Loro op (causal-history-wise); `pending_op_count() *
  1015	    ///   size_of_avg_op` is a memory floor for the not-yet-delivered
  1016	    ///   delta blob.
  1017	    ///
  1018	    /// # Semantic note — count includes peer ops AND undo ops
  1019	    ///
  1020	    /// The returned count is the magnitude of "VV entries the
  1021	    /// currently-attached transport hasn't seen," NOT "user's own
  1022	    /// unsynced edits." Includes BOTH local appends AND ops merged
  1023	    /// from peers since the last flush. **Includes undo ops** — each
  1024	    /// undo is a new causal-history entry (even though it retracts a
  1025	    /// visible op). For finer-grained "my net visible edits" an IDE
  1026	    /// builds its own peer-id-filtered counter — out of V2 V4 V1
  1027	    /// scope.
  1028	    ///
  1029	    /// # Edge cases
  1030	    ///
  1031	    /// - Fresh `CollabSession::new` session, no ops, no transport:
  1032	    ///   returns `0` (`current_vv == default`, `last_flushed_vv` is
  1033	    ///   `None.unwrap_or_default() = default`).
  1034	    /// - `from_snapshot` session: returns the imported VV's total
  1035	    ///   counter sum immediately, even before `attach_transport`.
  1036	    ///   Matches `has_pending_flush() == true` for the same scenario.
  1037	    /// - Post-`attach_transport`: baseline reset to `None`; count
  1038	    ///   includes ALL local ops (matches V2 V3 step 1 contract that
  1039	    ///   next flush sends from empty VV).
  1040	    /// - Post-successful-flush: baseline at `current_vv`; count `0`
  1041	    ///   (paired with `has_pending_flush() == false`).
  1042	    /// - Post-undo (with disabled auto-flush or no working transport):
  1043	    ///   count GROWS by 1 (the undo's inverse op is a new VV entry);
  1044	    ///   `has_pending_flush() == true`. The sibling relationship
  1045	    ///   `pending_op_count() > 0 ⟺ has_pending_flush() == true` holds
  1046	    ///   for all current mutators.
  1047	    pub fn pending_op_count(&self) -> usize {
  1048	        let current = self.log.oplog_vv();
  1049	        let last = self.last_flushed_vv.clone().unwrap_or_default();
  1050	        // Sum positive per-peer counter deltas. VV counters are
  1051	        // monotonic per peer in Loro's causal history, so
  1052	        // current[peer] >= last[peer] always holds; we use
  1053	        // `saturating_sub` as defensive insurance.
  1054	        let mut total: u64 = 0;
  1055	        for (peer, current_counter) in current.iter() {
  1056	            let last_counter = last.get(peer).copied().unwrap_or(0);
  1057	            let diff = (*current_counter as i64)
  1058	                .saturating_sub(last_counter as i64)
  1059	                .max(0) as u64;

  1061	        }
  1062	        total as usize
  1063	    }

   609	impl Drop for WebSocketTransport {
   610	    fn drop(&mut self) {
   611	        // **V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M2, 2026-05-21):** the
   612	        // sole shutdown path under current design is `abort()` on both
   613	        // task handles. The graceful `outbound_rx.recv() -> None ->
   614	        // ws_sink.close()` branch in the writer task is UNREACHABLE
   615	        // FROM DROP because `Drop::drop` runs before the struct's
   616	        // fields drop (Rust drop order: body first, then fields in
   617	        // decl order). So `outbound_tx` is still alive when we call
   618	        // `writer_task.abort()`. The graceful arm only fires if a
   619	        // future "soft close" API explicitly detaches `outbound_tx`
   620	        // before drop — not part of the current MVP.
   621	        //
   622	        // `closed = true` ordering: set first so any concurrent
   623	        // sync `send`/`try_recv` observes Closed via the flag check
   624	        // before the task abort propagates.
   625	        //
   626	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** also notify the
   627	        // flush_pending Condvar — a caller awaiting a long-running
   628	        // flush would otherwise wait until the next wait_timeout
   629	        // tick to observe the closed flag. (Unreachable in practice
   630	        // because Drop is called on a unique `&mut self` so no
   631	        // concurrent flush_pending can be in flight, but kept for
   632	        // safety + future shared-reference APIs.)
   633	        self.closed.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   634	        self.progress.1.notify_all();
   635	        self.writer_task.abort();
   636	        self.reader_task.abort();
   637	    }
   638	}

   640	impl Transport for WebSocketTransport {
   641	    fn send(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
   642	        // **LOAD-BEARING** (V2 V3 step 4 audit closure, Opus M4): this
   643	        // closed-flag check MUST precede `outbound_tx.send`. The
   644	        // `collab_session_websocket_send_after_close_surfaces_closed`
   645	        // integration test depends on observing `Closed` here (the
   646	        // reader task sets `closed = true` on peer disconnect; the
   647	        // writer task may still be parked on `outbound_rx.recv` and
   648	        // hasn't yet seen the broken sink). If a future refactor
   649	        // reorders this check (e.g., to enable an outbox-queuing-
   650	        // while-closed feature), that test will flake.
   651	        if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   652	            return Err(TransportError::Closed);
   653	        }
   654	        // UnboundedSender::send returns Err iff the receiver dropped.
   655	        // The receiver lives in the writer task; if it dropped, the
   656	        // task exited (panic, abort, or graceful). Treat as Closed.
   657	        self.outbound_tx
   658	            .send(bytes.to_vec())
   659	            .map_err(|_| TransportError::Closed)?;
   660	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   661	        // Bump the queued-count counter AFTER successful mpsc enqueue.
   662	        // flush_pending() reads this as the target the writer task
   663	        // must catch up to.
   664	        self.queued_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
   665	        Ok(())
   666	    }

   668	    fn try_recv(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, TransportError> {
   669	        // Drain-before-close per `Transport` trait contract
   670	        // (transport.rs:112-115): "Closed only when channel
   671	        // permanently closed AND internal queue is empty."
   672	        use mpsc::error::TryRecvError;
   673	        match self.inbound_rx.try_recv() {
   674	            Ok(bytes) => Ok(Some(bytes)),
   675	            Err(TryRecvError::Empty) => {
   676	                if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   677	                    Err(TransportError::Closed)
   678	                } else {
   679	                    Ok(None)
   680	                }
   681	            }
   682	            Err(TryRecvError::Disconnected) => {
   683	                // Reader task exited and dropped inbound_tx. Mark
   684	                // closed so subsequent calls fast-path; treat as
   685	                // Closed for this call (the queue is empty AND the
   686	                // upstream is permanently gone).
   687	                self.closed.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
   688	                Err(TransportError::Closed)
   689	            }
   690	        }
   691	    }

   702	    /// (`"WebSocket runtime error: ..."`) to detect the variant —
