   709	    /// **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) — Tier K1 ack channel.**
   710	    /// Block until every byte blob previously queued via `send` has
   711	    /// been written to the WebSocket sink. Closes the V2 V3 step 5
   712	    /// megaudit's convergent finding (queued-vs-acked semantics).
   713	    ///
   714	    /// Mechanism: reads `queued_count` as the target; locks the
   715	    /// `progress.0` counter and uses `Condvar::wait_timeout` to wake
   716	    /// every 100ms (so closed-flag transitions are observed promptly).
   717	    /// The writer task increments `progress.0` + `notify_all` after
   718	    /// each successful `ws_sink.send`, AND `notify_all` on closed-
   719	    /// flag transitions.
   720	    ///
   721	    /// # Errors
   722	    /// - `TransportError::Closed` if the transport was already closed
   723	    ///   on entry, OR if the writer task sets closed mid-wait (e.g.,
   724	    ///   ws_sink.send failed).
   725	    /// - `TransportError::Io` if the progress mutex is poisoned by a
   726	    ///   panicked writer task. The poisoned-mutex recovery via
   727	    ///   `PoisonError::into_inner()` is intentionally NOT used here:
   728	    ///   if the writer panicked mid-counter-increment, the counter
   729	    ///   may be in an inconsistent state (e.g., notify_all happened
   730	    ///   before counter increment); reading + retrying could
   731	    ///   busy-loop forever. Surface as Io and let the caller
   732	    ///   recover via reconnect.
   733	    fn flush_pending(&mut self) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
   734	        // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 audit closure (Codex M1, 2026-05-21):**
   735	        // honor the documented contract — if the transport is closed
   736	        // on entry, return Err(Closed) immediately, regardless of
   737	        // whether the local progress counter has already caught up.
   738	        // The prior impl returned Ok in this case, contradicting the
   739	        // docstring + the closed-on-entry test which now accepts
   740	        // both Ok and Err. After this closure, the contract is "Err
   741	        // if closed at any point — entry or mid-wait".
   742	        if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   743	            return Err(TransportError::Closed);
   744	        }
   745	        let target = self.queued_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
   746	        let (counter_lock, cv) = &*self.progress;
   747	        let mut counter = counter_lock
   748	            .lock()
   749	            .map_err(|e| TransportError::Io(format!("flush_pending lock poisoned: {e}")))?;
   750	        while *counter < target {
   751	            if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   752	                return Err(TransportError::Closed);
   753	            }
   754	            let (new_counter, _timeout_result) = cv
   755	                .wait_timeout(counter, Duration::from_millis(100))
   756	                .map_err(|e| TransportError::Io(format!("flush_pending wait poisoned: {e}")))?;
   757	            counter = new_counter;
   758	        }
   759	        Ok(())
   760	    }

   480	    pub fn attach_transport(&self, transport: &mut Transport) -> Result<()> {
   481	        let boxed = transport.take_inner().ok_or_else(|| {
   482	            // V2.1 audit closure (Codex LOW-1, 2026-05-22): error wording
   483	            // standardized. A "spent LoopbackPair" throws at takeA/takeB
   484	            // BEFORE producing a Transport — so a consumed Transport
   485	            // wrapper must have come from attachTransport (or a future
   486	            // consumer added in V2.3+).
   487	            Error::from_reason("Transport has already been consumed by attachTransport".to_string())
   488	        })?;
   489	        // attach_transport_boxed handles baseline-reset + replacement.
   490	        // The Option<Box> it returns is the PRIOR transport; we drop
   491	        // it here intentionally (see method docstring).
   492	        let mut inner = self.inner.lock();
   493	        let _prior = inner.attach_transport_boxed(boxed);
   494	        Ok(())
   495	    }

   541	    /// Drain inbound BLOBS from the attached transport (single-pass).

   551	    /// across LoopbackPair" found this empirically (asserting `>= 3`
   552	    /// failed against the actual blob-count semantics). The variable
   553	    /// names + JSDoc here now use "blobs" consistently.
   554	    ///
   555	    /// V2.1 ships the un-limited variant (engine default cap = 64).

   560	    /// fires one delta flush back through the transport (idempotency
   561	    /// guard prevents echo loops). V2.1 doesn't bind AutoFlushPolicy yet
   562	    /// — V2.2 does.

   574	        Ok(u32::try_from(blobs_drained).unwrap_or(u32::MAX))

   581	    /// Delta flush to the attached transport. Sends ONLY the ops added
   582	    /// since the last successful flush (via Loro's `ExportMode::Updates`
   583	    /// from this session's `last_flushed_vv`). Returns `true` if bytes
   584	    /// were actually sent.
   585	    ///
   586	    /// **This is the production default**; prefer it over
   587	    /// `flushToTransport` (full-snapshot) which is O(full state). Delta
   588	    /// flushes are O(per-op delta).
   589	    ///
   590	    /// **Idempotency short-circuit**: if `last_flushed_vv == Some(current)`
   591	    /// — i.e., a previous flush already advanced the baseline to the
   592	    /// current state — returns `Ok(false)` without invoking
   593	    /// `transport.send`. Closes the V2 V2 audit echo-loop concern.
   594	    ///
   595	    /// **First flush after attach ALWAYS sends** even on an empty op
   596	    /// log: attach resets `last_flushed_vv = None`, so the idempotency
   597	    /// guard (which checks `Some(last_vv) == current_vv`) is bypassed.
   598	    /// The first call encodes from the empty VV — for an empty op log
   599	    /// this is a small baseline blob; for a non-empty log it's the
   600	    /// full state. V2.2 mocha test
   601	    /// `flushDeltaToTransport second call with no state change
   602	    /// short-circuits to false` pins this exact contract.
   603	    ///
   604	    /// **Per Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 1 contract**: attach_transport resets
   605	    /// the per-session-per-transport `last_flushed_vv` to None. The
   606	    /// next call to `flushDeltaToTransport` after an attach sends from
   607	    /// the empty VV — delivering ALL local ops including any appended
   608	    /// while offline (Loro's CRDT op log IS the implicit offline queue).
   609	    ///
   610	    /// **Failure modes**:
   611	    /// - No transport attached → returns `Ok(false)` (NOT an error).
   612	    /// - Transport's `send` returns `Err(TransportError::*)` → JS Error.
   613	    #[napi(js_name = "flushDeltaToTransport")]
   614	    pub fn flush_delta_to_transport(&self) -> Result<bool> {
   615	        let mut inner = self.inner.lock();
   616	        inner
   617	            .flush_delta_to_transport()
   618	            .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("{e}")))
   619	    }
   620	
   621	    /// Like `pollRemote` but with an explicit cap on the number of
   622	    /// blobs to drain per call. Returns the number of BLOBS drained
   623	    /// (NOT ops), `<= limit`.
   624	    ///
   625	    /// **Limit semantics** (per engine docstring):
   626	    /// - `limit == 0` → no-op, returns `Ok(0)` even if blobs queued.
   627	    /// - If the returned count equals `limit`, more blobs may still
   628	    ///   be queued — call again.
   629	    /// - If less, the queue drained (either empty or transport
   630	    ///   reported `Closed`).
   631	    ///
   632	    /// **Input validation** (per V1 megaudit closure pattern):
   633	    /// `limit` takes `f64` to avoid napi-rs's `napi_get_value_uint32`
   634	    /// ECMAScript ToUint32 silent coercion (`-1 → u32::MAX`, etc.).
   635	    /// Validated finite + non-negative + integer + in `usize` range
   636	    /// (on 64-bit systems usize = u64; we cap at u32::MAX for cross-
   637	    /// platform safety).
   638	    ///
   639	    /// **Failure modes**:
   640	    /// - No transport attached → returns `Ok(0)`.
   641	    /// - `limit` not a finite non-negative integer in u32 range → JS Error.
   642	    /// - Transport's `try_recv` returns `Err` → JS Error.
   643	    #[napi(js_name = "pollRemoteWithLimit")]
   644	    pub fn poll_remote_with_limit(&self, limit: f64) -> Result<u32> {
   645	        let limit_u32 = validate_u32_index("pollRemoteWithLimit", "limit", limit)?;
   646	        let mut inner = self.inner.lock();
   647	        let blobs_drained = inner
   648	            .poll_remote_with_limit(limit_u32 as usize)
   649	            .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("{e}")))?;
   650	        Ok(u32::try_from(blobs_drained).unwrap_or(u32::MAX))
   651	    }

   677	    /// Set the auto-flush policy. Returns the prior policy.
   678	    ///
   679	    /// **Accepted strings**: `"disabled"` (default) or `"onAppend"`.
   680	    /// Any other string returns a JS Error listing the accepted values.
   681	    ///
   682	    /// **`"onAppend"` semantics** (Phase 5.5 V2 V2 + V2 V3 steps 1+2):
   683	    /// every public mutator (`append_op`, `merge_bytes`,
   684	    /// `update_presence`, `clear_presence`, `sweep_presence`, `undo`,
   685	    /// `redo`, `poll_remote`, `poll_remote_with_limit`) auto-fires a
   686	    /// delta flush after the mutation. Idempotency short-circuits
   687	    /// no-op state changes; `poll_remote*` fires the flush once after
   688	    /// the batch (not per-blob).
   689	    ///
   690	    /// **Why string union over enum**: napi-rs binds Rust enums as
   691	    /// JS objects with a discriminant field, which is verbose for
   692	    /// 2-variant enums. The string-union approach is JS-idiomatic and
   693	    /// easy to test. Forward-compat: the engine's `AutoFlushPolicy`
   694	    /// is `#[non_exhaustive]` so future variants won't break this
   695	    /// binding — they'll just be unparseable by this method until V2.3+
   696	    /// adds string mappings.
   697	    ///
   698	    /// **Accepted alias forms (engine-side leniency)**: the engine
   699	    /// parser also accepts `"Disabled"`, `"OnAppend"`, `"on-append"`
   700	    /// as aliases for the canonical camelCase. The return value is
   701	    /// always canonical camelCase. JS callers SHOULD pass the
   702	    /// canonical forms (`"disabled"` / `"onAppend"`) only; the IDE-side
   703	    /// `isAutoFlushPolicy` type guard enforces this on the TS side
   704	    /// (rejects aliases). The lenient parser exists for engine-
   705	    /// internal callers and config-file backward-compat — not as a
   706	    /// public IDE contract. V2.2 audit closure (Opus HIGH-2): the
   707	    /// alias-acceptance is NOT pinned by the IDE mocha tests; engine-
   708	    /// side tests cover the parser.
   709	    ///
   710	    /// **Partial-state error contract (Codex MEDIUM-3 closure)**:
   711	    /// under `onAppend`, a mutator call sequence is "1. commit local
   712	    /// op → 2. flush to transport". If step 2 throws
   713	    /// `Error("transport closed")`, the local op is ALREADY committed
   714	    /// (step 1 succeeded). IDE retry logic must:
   715	    /// - NOT retry the original mutation (would duplicate the op).
   716	    /// - Reconnect the transport + call `flushDeltaToTransport`
   717	    ///   explicitly to flush the pending op.
   718	    /// V2.3+ will add structured `Error.code` discrimination so this
   719	    /// retry-shape is machine-readable; until then, the IDE must
   720	    /// substring-match `"transport"` in the error message.
   721	    #[napi(js_name = "setAutoFlushPolicy")]
   722	    pub fn set_auto_flush_policy(&self, policy: String) -> Result<String> {
   723	        let policy_enum = parse_auto_flush_policy(&policy)?;
   724	        let mut inner = self.inner.lock();
   725	        let prior = inner.set_auto_flush_policy(policy_enum);
   726	        // V2.2 audit closure (Opus HIGH-1): auto_flush_policy_to_string
   727	        // now returns Result and throws on unknown variants. Propagate
   728	        // the Result.
   729	        auto_flush_policy_to_string(prior)
   730	    }

   893	
   894	/// JS-facing opaque wrapper for a `Box<dyn ql_collab::Transport + Send>`.
   895	///
   896	/// **Design rationale (Phase 5.7 V1 megaudit Opus-B HIGH-2 closure,
   897	/// 2026-05-22)**: napi-rs cannot bind generic functions. The engine's
   898	/// `CollabSession::attach_transport<T>` accepts any `T: Transport + Send +
   899	/// 'static`. To make this reachable from JS we:
   900	///   1. Added `CollabSession::attach_transport_boxed(Box<dyn Transport + Send>)`
   901	///      on the Rust side as a sibling entry point (V2.1 cycle).
   902	///   2. Expose this opaque `Transport` class wrapping the boxed trait
   903	///      object. JS code obtains instances from static factories
   904	///      (`Transport.loopbackPair()` here; `Transport.websocketConnect(url)`
   905	///      in V2.3) and passes them to `CollabSession.attachTransport(t)`.
   906	///
   907	/// **Single-use semantics**: an instance owns its boxed trait object.
   908	/// `CollabSession.attachTransport` MOVES the box out of this wrapper,
   909	/// leaving it consumed. Subsequent attach calls with the same wrapper
   910	/// return a JS Error ("Transport has already been consumed by attachTransport").
   911	/// This mirrors Rust ownership semantics within the constraint that JS
   912	/// doesn't have a move primitive.
   913	///
   914	/// **Why opaque (no introspection methods)**: the inner `Box<dyn Transport>`
   915	/// is a fat pointer to one of several impls (Loopback, WebSocket, ...).
   916	/// V2.1 doesn't expose impl-specific accessors; future versions can add
   917	/// `kind() -> string` if a use case emerges.
   918	#[napi]
   919	pub struct Transport {
   920	    // `Option` so we can move the inner Box out at attach time without
   921	    // dropping the wrapper. napi-rs's class instance has `&mut self`
   922	    // discipline (per V1 module docs Send+!Sync rationale) — we cannot
   923	    // consume `self` from a `#[napi]` method, only take from an Option.
   924	    inner: Option<Box<dyn CoreTransport + Send>>,
   925	}
   926	
   927	#[napi]
   928	impl Transport {
   929	    /// `true` while this wrapper still owns its inner transport (not yet
   930	    /// passed to `attachTransport`). Useful for IDE code that wants to
   931	    /// branch on whether a Transport instance is still usable without
   932	    /// catching an exception.
   933	    #[napi(js_name = "isAttachable")]
   934	    pub fn is_attachable(&self) -> bool {
   935	        self.inner.is_some()
   936	    }

   938	    // ==========================================================
   939	    // Phase 5.7 V2.3 (2026-05-22) — async WebSocket factory
   940	    // ==========================================================
   941	
   942	    /// Connect to a WebSocket peer and return a Transport wrapping the
   943	    /// resulting `WebSocketTransport`. Returns a JS `Promise<Transport>`.
   944	    ///
   945	    /// **URL format**: standard `ws://host:port` (no TLS in V2.3 — V2.4+
   946	    /// will add `wss://` once the engine's `ql-collab-ws` exposes TLS).
   947	    ///
   948	    /// **Failure modes** (all surface as JS Promise rejections):
   949	    /// - `WebSocketError::InvalidUrl` — URL parse failed.
   950	    /// - `WebSocketError::ConnectFailed` — TCP/DNS error.
   951	    /// - `WebSocketError::HandshakeFailed` — WS upgrade rejected
   952	    ///   (e.g., HTTP 401, protocol mismatch).
   953	    ///
   954	    /// **Lifecycle**: the returned Transport instance owns a
   955	    /// `WebSocketTransport` with two background tokio tasks
   956	    /// (reader + writer). On detach, the tasks are aborted via the
   957	    /// engine's `WebSocketTransport::Drop`. Don't hold the Transport
   958	    /// past detach (V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure pattern).
   959	    ///
   960	    /// **napi-rs async pattern**: `#[napi]` on `async fn` runs the
   961	    /// body on a tokio task spawned from napi-rs's built-in runtime
   962	    /// (gated by the `async` feature in the workspace `Cargo.toml`).
   963	    /// The Promise resolves on the V8 thread once the async fn
   964	    /// completes — no manual ThreadsafeFunction plumbing needed.
   965	    #[napi(js_name = "websocketConnect")]
   966	    pub async fn websocket_connect(url: String) -> Result<Transport> {
   967	        let ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&url)
   968	            .await
   969	            .map_err(|e| Error::from_reason(format!("{e}")))?;
   970	        Ok(Transport {
   971	            inner: Some(Box::new(ws)),
   972	        })
   973	    }
   974	}
   975	
   976	impl Transport {
   977	    /// **`pub(crate)` — only the napi `CollabSession::attach_transport`
   978	    /// method should call this.** Move the inner Box out for attach.
   979	    /// Called by the napi method, NOT the Rust generic
   980	    /// `ql_collab::CollabSession::attach_transport`. After this returns
   981	    /// `Some`, the wrapper is consumed; subsequent `is_attachable`
   982	    /// returns `false` and the inner box has been handed off.
   983	    ///
   984	    /// **V2.1 audit closure (Opus LOW-4, 2026-05-22)**: the prior
   985	    /// docstring said "Rust-only" which could be misread as private to
   986	    /// this `impl` block. `pub(crate)` IS the visibility — but calling
   987	    /// from any site other than `CollabSession::attach_transport`
   988	    /// silently consumes the wrapper without an `attach`-paired side
   989	    /// effect. Future contributors: do NOT call this from anywhere
   990	    /// else.
   991	    pub(crate) fn take_inner(&mut self) -> Option<Box<dyn CoreTransport + Send>> {
   992	        self.inner.take()
   993	    }
   994	}
   995	
   996	/// Two-ended in-process Transport pair (LoopbackTransport).
   997	///
   998	/// JS callers use this as a stepping-stone to obtain the two `Transport`
   999	/// instances that share a Loopback queue:
  1000	///
  1001	/// ```ignore
  1002	/// const pair = new LoopbackPair();
  1003	/// const transportA = pair.takeA();
  1004	/// const transportB = pair.takeB();
  1005	/// sessionA.attachTransport(transportA);
  1006	/// sessionB.attachTransport(transportB);
  1007	/// ```
  1008	///
  1009	/// **Why this intermediate class** (Phase 5.7 V2.1 design note,
  1010	/// 2026-05-22): napi-rs's `#[napi(factory, ...)]` can only return a
  1011	/// single `Self`-typed class instance. Returning a 2-tuple or
  1012	/// `Vec<Transport>` fails the trait bound `ObjectFinalize` napi-rs
  1013	/// imposes on factory returns. The cleanest pattern that keeps each
  1014	/// `Transport` end as a separately-attachable class is to expose the
  1015	/// pair-creation step as its own short-lived class with two takers.
  1016	///
  1017	/// **Single-use takers**: each of `takeA` / `takeB` can be called once
  1018	/// per `LoopbackPair` instance. Calling a second time on the same end
  1019	/// returns a JS Error. (Calling a non-yet-taken end after the other has
  1020	/// been taken still works — the two ends are independent.)
  1021	#[napi]
  1022	pub struct LoopbackPair {
  1023	    // Both ends live here until taken. The pair is constructed eagerly
  1024	    // in `new()` so the shared queue exists before either end is
  1025	    // distributed.
  1026	    a: Option<LoopbackTransport>,
  1027	    b: Option<LoopbackTransport>,
  1028	}
  1029	
  1030	impl Default for LoopbackPair {
  1030	impl Default for LoopbackPair {
  1031	    fn default() -> Self {
  1032	        Self::new()
  1033	    }
  1034	}
  1035	
  1036	#[napi]
  1037	impl LoopbackPair {
  1038	    /// Construct a fresh Loopback pair. Both ends start un-taken.
  1039	    #[napi(constructor)]
  1040	    pub fn new() -> Self {
  1041	        let (a, b) = LoopbackTransport::pair();
  1042	        Self {
  1043	            a: Some(a),
  1044	            b: Some(b),
  1045	        }
  1046	    }
  1047	
  1048	    /// Take ownership of end A. Errors if already taken.

   293	/// **Phase 5.5 V1 (2026-05-19):** in-process paired `Transport`
   294	/// impl for 2-peer round-trip testing.
   295	///
   296	/// Constructed via [`LoopbackTransport::pair`]: returns two
   297	/// endpoints `(a, b)` where `a.send(bytes)` lands in `b`'s recv
   298	/// queue and vice versa. The two endpoints share two
   299	/// `Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>>` channels via interior
   300	/// mutability — `Send + Sync` so they can also be used across
   301	/// threads if a future test wants that.
   302	///
   303	/// ## Use case
   304	///
   305	/// Wire two `CollabSession`s together for tests like:
   306	/// ```ignore
   307	/// let (mut tx_a, mut tx_b) = LoopbackTransport::pair();
   308	/// let session_a = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1))?;
   309	/// let session_b = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(2))?;
   310	/// // ... append ops on a, drain via tx_a.send / tx_b.try_recv ...
   311	/// ```
   312	///
   313	/// **Phase 5.5 V2 V2 (2026-05-21):** `CollabSession` supports
   314	/// opt-in auto-flush via `AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend` — every
   315	/// session mutator (`append_op`, `merge_bytes`, presence writes,
   316	/// `undo` / `redo` when consumed, `sweep_presence`) then sends
   317	/// through the attached transport automatically. Default policy
   318	/// remains `Disabled` (V2 V1 explicit-drive behavior). Tests can
   319	/// still drive the flow manually: append, export_bytes, send via
   320	/// the transport, recv on the other side, merge_bytes — useful
   321	/// when the test wants deterministic control over when bytes
   322	/// land on the wire (e.g. ordering tests). **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 2
   323	/// (2026-05-21):** `poll_remote*` now also triggers auto-flush after
   324	/// a non-empty drain (one flush per call, not per-blob). See
   325	/// [`crate::AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend`] for the receive-side
   326	/// contract.
   327	///
   328	/// ## Close semantics
   329	///
   330	/// Each endpoint has its OWN `closed` flag (separate
   331	/// `AtomicBool`). `a.close()` shuts down endpoint A:
   332	/// - A's `send` returns `TransportError::Closed` immediately.
   333	/// - A's `try_recv` drains any already-queued bytes FIRST and
   334	///   only returns `Closed` once the queue is empty (per the
   335	///   `Transport` trait contract at the trait docstring).
   336	/// - B is unaffected: B can still `send` (bytes land in A's
   337	///   inbox; A drains them on the next try_recv before reporting
   338	///   Closed) and `try_recv` (drains B's inbox).
   339	///
   340	/// ## Atomic ordering caveat
   341	///
   342	/// `close` uses `AtomicBool` with `Relaxed` ordering. For
   343	/// cross-thread "close then send" semantics, callers must use
   344	/// external synchronization — a thread that observes
   345	/// `is_closed() == true` after another thread's `close()` is NOT
   346	/// guaranteed by this transport alone (the atomic only protects
   347	/// the flag itself, not the surrounding sequence).
   348	pub struct LoopbackTransport {
   349	    /// Channel WE drain via `try_recv`. The peer's `send` writes
   350	    /// here.
   351	    inbox: Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>>,
   352	    /// Channel WE write to via `send`. The peer's `try_recv`
   353	    /// drains here.
   354	    outbox: Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<Vec<u8>>>>,
   355	    /// Per-endpoint close flag. Atomic so `close(&self)` doesn't
   356	    /// need `&mut`.
   357	    closed: AtomicBool,
   358	}

   379	    /// `b.send(...)` enqueues to `a.try_recv()`.
   380	    pub fn pair() -> (Self, Self) {
   381	        let a_to_b = Arc::new(Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()));
   382	        let b_to_a = Arc::new(Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()));

   391	            closed: AtomicBool::new(false),
   392	        };

   394	    }

   400	    pub fn close(&self) {

   418	impl Transport for LoopbackTransport {
   419	    fn send(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
   420	        if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   421	            return Err(TransportError::Closed);
   422	        }
   423	        self.outbox
   424	            .lock()
   425	            .map_err(|e| TransportError::Io(format!("loopback outbox lock poisoned: {e}")))?
   426	            .push_back(bytes.to_vec());
   427	        Ok(())
   428	    }
   429	
   430	    fn try_recv(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, TransportError> {
   431	        // Trait contract (transport.rs:71-74): "Closed only when the
   432	        // channel is permanently closed AND its internal queue is
   433	        // empty." So drain any already-queued bytes first; only
   434	        // return Closed when both closed AND drained.
   435	        // Codex + Opus 5.5 V1 audit MEDIUM/HIGH closure: pre-closure
   436	        // we returned Closed immediately on close, violating the
   437	        // contract.
   438	        let mut queue = self
   439	            .inbox
   440	            .lock()
   441	            .map_err(|e| TransportError::Io(format!("loopback inbox lock poisoned: {e}")))?;
   442	        if let Some(bytes) = queue.pop_front() {
   443	            return Ok(Some(bytes));
   444	        }
   445	        // Queue empty — now distinguish "open but empty" from "closed".
   446	        if self.closed.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
   447	            Err(TransportError::Closed)
   448	        } else {
   449	            Ok(None)
   450	        }
   451	    }
   452	}

  1262	        // `last_flushed_vv` to current. The peer now has everything
  1263	        // up to this VV; subsequent `flush_delta_to_transport` calls
  1264	        // send only ops appended AFTER this point. Without this
  1265	        // update, a mixed-call sequence (`flush_to_transport` then

  1273	    /// **Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 1 (2026-05-21):** export and send the
  1274	    /// DELTA of ops added since the last successful flush to the
  1275	    /// attached transport. Returns `Ok(true)` if bytes were sent,
  1276	    /// `Ok(false)` if no transport is attached OR if no ops have
  1277	    /// been appended since the last flush (idempotency short-
  1278	    /// circuit — closes V2 V2 audit M2/M3 echo-loop class for
  1279	    /// step 2's `poll_remote` auto-flush wiring).
  1280	    ///
  1281	    /// Wire bytes are `LoroDoc::ExportMode::Updates { from: last_flushed_vv }`.
  1282	    /// The first flush after `attach_transport` (or after `new`)
  1283	    /// sends from the empty VV — equivalent to `all_updates()` —
  1284	    /// delivering the full history to the new transport-peer.
  1285	    /// Subsequent flushes send only the delta since the prior flush.
  1286	    ///
  1287	    /// Loro's `LoroDoc::import` transparently consumes both
  1288	    /// `Snapshot` and `Updates` blobs, so the wire format is opaque
  1289	    /// to peers — switching from snapshots to deltas is a
  1290	    /// SENDER-SIDE optimization with NO PEER-SIDE CHANGES required.
  1291	    ///
  1292	    /// # Mix-and-match with `flush_to_transport`
  1293	    ///
  1294	    /// Both APIs maintain the SHARED `last_flushed_vv` field, so
  1295	    /// callers can interleave full snapshots and deltas freely. A
  1296	    /// typical pattern:
  1297	    /// - Initial handshake: `flush_to_transport` to seed the peer
  1298	    ///   with full state.
  1299	    /// - Steady state under `OnAppend`: `maybe_auto_flush` (via
  1300	    ///   `flush_delta_to_transport`) sends tiny deltas per
  1301	    ///   mutation.
  1302	    /// - On peer reconnect: caller may choose to `flush_to_transport`
  1303	    ///   again as a safety net (Loro deduplicates on import; no
  1304	    ///   harm even if the peer already has those ops).
  1305	    ///
  1306	    /// # Error handling
  1307	    ///
  1308	    /// Same partial-state contract as `flush_to_transport`:
  1309	    /// - `CollabSessionError::OpLog` on `export_delta_bytes` failure.
  1310	    /// - `CollabSessionError::Transport` on `send` failure (Closed, Io).
  1311	    /// - `last_flushed_vv` is NOT updated on `Err` — a retry sends
  1312	    ///   the same delta the failed call would have sent.
  1313	    ///
  1314	    /// # Delivery semantics — queued vs acked
  1315	    ///
  1316	    /// **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Codex M1 + Opus-B M1,
  1317	    /// 2026-05-21):** "successful flush" means
  1318	    /// [`Transport::send`] returned `Ok` — which, per the trait
  1319	    /// contract, means bytes are **queued for send** to the currently-
  1320	    /// attached transport. For buffered async impls
  1321	    /// (`WebSocketTransport`), the bytes sit in an internal mpsc
  1322	    /// channel until the background writer task pushes them to the
  1323	    /// WebSocket sink. **`last_flushed_vv` advances at queue-success,
  1324	    /// not at wire-delivery confirmation.**
  1325	    ///
  1326	    /// Concrete consequences:
  1327	    /// - `has_pending_flush() == false` AFTER a successful flush means
  1328	    ///   "queued to the currently-attached transport," NOT "the peer
  1329	    ///   has received the ops."
  1330	    /// - If the transport is dropped between queue and wire (e.g., tab
  1331	    ///   close, app shutdown, transport panic), the in-flight bytes
  1332	    ///   are lost silently and the peer never receives them.
  1333	    /// - Recovery from transport drop is the same as recovery from
  1334	    ///   `Err(Closed)`: detach + reattach a new transport. The V2 V3
  1335	    ///   step 1 baseline-reset re-sends from empty VV — all ops are
  1335	    ///   step 1 baseline-reset re-sends from empty VV — all ops are
  1336	    ///   redelivered, including the previously-"flushed" ones the
  1337	    ///   prior transport never put on the wire.
  1338	    ///
  1339	    /// For IDE consumers building "safe to close window?" workflows,
  1340	    /// the `has_pending_flush() == false` signal is insufficient on
  1341	    /// its own. **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (2026-05-21) Tier K1 closure**:
  1342	    /// call [`Self::flush_pending_to_transport`] after this method
  1343	    /// to block until the writer task has completed `ws_sink.send`
  1344	    /// for every queued blob — level-1 (local writer) ack. For
  1345	    /// TCP-level or peer-application-level ack, build a custom ack-op
  1346	    /// layered on `merge_bytes` (out of scope for V2 V4 V1).
  1347	    pub fn flush_delta_to_transport(&mut self) -> Result<bool, CollabSessionError> {
  1348	        if self.transport.is_none() {
  1349	            return Ok(false);
  1350	        }
  1351	        let current_vv = self.log.oplog_vv();
  1352	        // Idempotency short-circuit: no state change since last flush.
  1353	        // Closes V2 V2 audit M2/M3 (echo-loop). NOTE: VersionVector
  1354	        // equality is by value (Loro impls PartialEq via the
  1355	        // underlying op count per peer); a session that hasn't
  1356	        // appended/merged anything since the prior flush returns
  1357	        // Ok(false) without invoking transport.send.
  1358	        if let Some(last_vv) = self.last_flushed_vv.as_ref() {
  1359	            if last_vv == &current_vv {
  1360	                return Ok(false);
  1361	            }
  1362	        }
  1363	        // Encode delta bytes. `from = last_flushed_vv` (or empty if None).
  1364	        let bytes = match self.last_flushed_vv.as_ref() {
  1365	            Some(from) => self.log.export_delta_bytes(from)?,
  1366	            None => self
  1367	                .log
  1368	                .export_delta_bytes(&loro::VersionVector::default())?,
  1369	        };
  1370	        // Now borrow transport mutably for the send. Done in two
  1371	        // phases because we needed self.log (immut) above and need
  1372	        // self.transport (mut) here — borrow-checker dance.
  1373	        let transport = self.transport.as_mut().expect("just-checked is_some above");
  1374	        transport.send(&bytes)?;
  1375	        // Advance the VV checkpoint. Only on success — Err leaves
  1376	        // last_flushed_vv at its prior value so retry sends the
  1377	        // same delta.
  1378	        self.last_flushed_vv = Some(current_vv);
  1379	        Ok(true)
  1380	    }

     1	//! Phase 5.5 V2 V2 (2026-05-21) — auto-flush on append integration tests.
     2	//!
     3	//! Verifies `CollabSession::set_auto_flush_policy(AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend)`
     4	//! propagates every local mutation through the attached transport
     5	//! WITHOUT a manual `flush_to_transport` call.
     6	//!
     7	//! V2 V1 (Phase 5.5 V2 V1 ship `ffd8f6e5f05`) was deliberately
     8	//! explicit-drive: caller invokes `flush_to_transport()` after each
     9	//! batch. V2 V2 adds the opt-in `OnAppend` policy so IDE callers
    10	//! (Phase 5.7) can rely on "every keystroke propagates" without
    11	//! scheduling their own flush ticks.
    12	//!
    13	//! ## Coverage
    14	//!
    15	//! - Default policy is `Disabled` (V2 V1 behavior preserved).
    16	//! - `OnAppend` with no transport: append_op succeeds; no error.
    17	//! - `OnAppend` with LoopbackTransport pair: appends propagate without
    18	//!   manual flush.
    19	//! - `OnAppend` with closed transport: append_op surfaces Err with
    20	//!   local op already committed (partial-state contract).
    21	//! - Auto-flush triggers on every documented mutator: `append_op`,
    22	//!   `merge_bytes`, `update_presence`, `clear_presence`,
    23	//!   `sweep_presence`, `undo`, `redo`.
    24	//! - Policy round-trip: set_auto_flush_policy returns previous,
    25	//!   subsequent auto_flush_policy() reflects new value.
    26	//! - Flip back to Disabled stops flushing.

    97	// (Counting per-mutator sends is covered by LoopbackTransport's

   101	
   102	#[test]
   103	fn on_append_propagates_via_loopback_pair() {
   104	    // Peer A: policy OnAppend, transport attached.
   105	    // Peer B: holds the paired transport endpoint (NO session — we just
   106	    //         drain via try_recv to verify peer A's auto-flush sent bytes).
   107	    let (tx_a, mut tx_b) = LoopbackTransport::pair();
   108	
   109	    let mut peer_a = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1)).unwrap();
   110	    peer_a.attach_transport(tx_a);
   111	    peer_a.set_auto_flush_policy(AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend);

   114

   116	    assert_eq!(

   118	        1,
   119	        "auto-flush MUST fire after append_op without manual flush_to_transport"
   120	    );

   122	    peer_a.append_op(put_value(0, 0, 0, 42.0)).unwrap();
   123	    assert_eq!(tx_b.pending_recv(), 2, "second append → second auto-flush");
   124	
   125	    // Drain tx_b: each blob must be a valid Loro snapshot (try_recv
   126	    // returns Some bytes).
   127	    let first = tx_b.try_recv().unwrap();
   128	    assert!(
   129	        first.is_some_and(|bytes| !bytes.is_empty()),
   130	        "auto-flushed bytes are non-empty Loro snapshot"
   131	    );
   132	    let second = tx_b.try_recv().unwrap();
   133	    assert!(second.is_some_and(|bytes| !bytes.is_empty()));
   134	    assert_eq!(tx_b.try_recv().unwrap(), None, "queue drained");

   257	    // that the previously-"failed-flush" op #2 (committed locally) is
   258	    // included in the next snapshot. Phase 5.5 V2 V2 audit closure
   259	    // Opus L2 (2026-05-21): pre-closure this test used NoopTransport
   260	    // and never asserted that op #2 appears post-reattach.
   261	    let _bad = s.detach_transport();
   262	    let (tx_fresh, mut fresh_observer) = LoopbackTransport::pair();
   263	    s.attach_transport(tx_fresh);
   264	    s.append_op(put_value(0, 1, 0, 2.0)).unwrap();
   265	    assert_eq!(s.op_count(), 3);

   267	    // Verify the recovered transport's peer sees a snapshot that
   268	    // contains BOTH op #2 (the "failed flush" op) and op #3. The
   269	    // V2 V2 full-snapshot semantics mean every flush carries the
   270	    // full local state from scratch, so the freshly-attached
   271	    // transport gets the complete log even though it joined late.
   272	    assert_eq!(
   273	        fresh_observer.pending_recv(),
   274	        1,
   275	        "post-reattach append MUST auto-flush onto the fresh transport"
   276	    );
   277	    let snap = fresh_observer.try_recv().unwrap().expect("snapshot bytes");
   278	    let recovered_log = ql_oplog::OpLog::import_bytes(&snap).unwrap();
   279	    assert_eq!(
   280	        recovered_log.len(),
   281	        3,
   282	        "full-snapshot flush MUST include op #1 (pre-failure) + op #2 (failed-flush op, committed locally) + op #3 (post-recovery)"

   284	
   285	    // Silence the original drop of tx_b detached.
   286	    let _ = detached;

   411	    // "receive-side excluded by design" exclusion. With V2 V3 step 1's

   417	    // OPPOSITE — now the contract is inverted): peer A has OnAppend +
   418	    // transport. Peer B sends a blob with a NEW op into A's inbox.
   419	    // A's poll_remote drains it AND auto-flushes the merged delta
   420	    // back onto the same paired transport. tx_b (B's side) sees the
   421	    // round-trip arrive.

   424	    peer_a.attach_transport(tx_a);

   428	    // op and pushes the bytes into A's inbox via the paired endpoint.

   430	    peer_b.append_op(add_sheet()).unwrap();

   436	        0,

   441	    // ALSO auto-flushes the post-merge delta back through the same
   442	    // transport — bytes land in B's inbox.

   445	    assert!(
   446	        peer_a.op_count() >= 1,
   447	        "A's log now contains B's op via the merge"
   448	    );
   449	    assert_eq!(
   450	        tx_b.pending_recv(),
   451	        1,
   452	        "V2 V3 step 2: poll_remote MUST auto-flush after a successful drain that advanced state"
   453	    );

   456	    let bytes_back = tx_b.try_recv().unwrap().expect("round-trip bytes");
   457	    let _imported = ql_oplog::OpLog::import_bytes(&bytes_back).unwrap();
   458	}

    37	/// Build a single-threaded tokio runtime for one test. Each test owns
    38	/// its runtime so panics + abort() cleanups can't leak across tests.
    39	fn runtime() -> tokio::runtime::Runtime {
    40	    tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread()
    41	        .enable_all()
    42	        .build()
    43	        .expect("build tokio runtime")

    46	/// **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** multi-thread runtime for tests that
    47	/// call sync `flush_pending()`. The single-threaded runtime above
    48	/// would deadlock because flush_pending blocks the worker thread via
    49	/// `Condvar::wait_timeout`, preventing the writer/reader tokio tasks
    50	/// from making progress. Multi-thread runtime gives the tokio tasks
    51	/// their own workers. This matches the documented async-context
    52	/// caveat in `Transport::flush_pending` — real IDE consumers either
    53	/// run on a multi-thread runtime OR wrap the call in
    54	/// `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`.
    55	fn multi_thread_runtime() -> tokio::runtime::Runtime {
    56	    tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread()
    57	        .worker_threads(2)
    58	        .enable_all()
    59	        .build()
    60	        .expect("build multi-thread tokio runtime")
    61	}

    63	/// Poll `try_recv` with short sleeps for up to `max_iters * 10ms`
    64	/// looking for a binary blob. Async background tasks need a chance
    65	/// to deliver bytes; tests block on this helper.
    66	async fn await_blob(transport: &mut WebSocketTransport, max_iters: u32) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    67	    for _ in 0..max_iters {
    68	        match transport.try_recv() {
    69	            Ok(Some(b)) => return Some(b),
    70	            Ok(None) => tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await,
    71	            Err(_) => return None,
    72	        }
    73	    }
    74	    None
    75	}

   212	#[test]
   213	fn explicit_close_drains_inbox_before_returning_closed() {
   214	    let rt = runtime();
   215	    rt.block_on(async {
   216	        // Trait contract (transport.rs:112-115): Closed only when
   217	        // permanently closed AND queue empty. Pre-load the inbox
   218	        // before close.
   219	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   220	        let mut ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   221	            .await
   222	            .expect("handshake");
   223	        ws.send(b"queued-before-close").expect("send");
   224	        // Let the echo + delivery happen.
   225	        let echoed = await_blob(&mut ws, 100).await.expect("echo delivered");
   226	        assert_eq!(echoed, b"queued-before-close".to_vec());
   227	        // Now send a second one, give it time to land in the inbox,
   228	        // close, then drain.
   229	        ws.send(b"queued-also").expect("send");
   230	        // Give the reader task a chance to receive it.
   231	        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
   232	        ws.close();
   233	        // Drain-before-close: first try_recv must return the blob,
   234	        // THEN return Closed once empty.
   235	        match ws.try_recv() {
   236	            Ok(Some(b)) => {
   237	                assert_eq!(b, b"queued-also".to_vec(), "drained blob is the queued one");
   238	                assert!(matches!(ws.try_recv(), Err(TransportError::Closed)));
   239	            }
   240	            Ok(None) => {
   240	            Ok(None) => {
   241	                // Race: reader task hadn't delivered yet. After more
   242	                // sleep, must EITHER deliver the blob (drain-before-close)
   243	                // OR return Closed because the channel is closed and
   244	                // the blob never landed.
   245	                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
   246	                let final_r = ws.try_recv();
   247	                assert!(
   248	                    matches!(final_r, Ok(Some(_)) | Err(TransportError::Closed)),
   249	                    "post-close try_recv must be Some or Closed, got {:?}",
   250	                    final_r
   251	                );
   252	            }
   253	            Err(_) => panic!("first try_recv after close should drain first"),
   254	        }
   255	    });
   256	}

   258	#[test]
   259	fn server_close_propagates_to_try_recv_as_closed() {
   260	    let rt = runtime();
   261	    rt.block_on(async {
   262	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   263	        let mut ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   264	            .await
   265	            .expect("handshake");
   266	        // Drop the server: accept task aborts; existing connection
   267	        // dies when its tokio scope ends. Reader task sees EOF / Err
   268	        // and marks closed.
   269	        drop(server);
   270	        // Give the reader task time to observe the disconnect.
   271	        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
   272	        // Subsequent send may succeed initially (writer task queued
   273	        // it) but the connection is gone. Loop try_recv until Closed.
   274	        let mut closed_observed = false;
   275	        for _ in 0..50 {
   276	            match ws.try_recv() {
   277	                Ok(None) => tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await,
   278	                Ok(Some(_)) => continue,
   279	                Err(TransportError::Closed) => {
   280	                    closed_observed = true;
   281	                    break;
   282	                }
   283	                Err(other) => panic!("unexpected error: {other:?}"),
   284	            }
   285	        }
   286	        assert!(
   287	            closed_observed,
   288	            "after server drop + grace, try_recv MUST eventually return Closed"
   289	        );
   290	    });
   291	}

   297	#[test]
   298	fn drop_aborts_background_tasks() {
   299	    let rt = runtime();
   300	    rt.block_on(async {
   301	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   302	        let ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   303	            .await
   304	            .expect("handshake");
   305	        // Snapshot whether tasks are still running.
   306	        assert!(!ws.is_closed());
   307	        let dbg_before = format!("{:?}", ws);
   308	        assert!(
   309	            dbg_before.contains("writer_finished: false"),
   310	            "writer task is running pre-drop: {dbg_before}"
   311	        );
   312	        assert!(
   313	            dbg_before.contains("reader_finished: false"),
   314	            "reader task is running pre-drop: {dbg_before}"
   315	        );
   316	        drop(ws);
   317	        // After drop, the spawned tasks are abort()ed. We can't
   318	        // re-introspect a dropped transport, but if the tasks weren't
   319	        // aborted they'd leak the tokio runtime past test end. The
   320	        // runtime drop on test exit would block. This test passing
   321	        // (i.e. the test function returning) is the assertion.
   322	    });
   323	}

   329	#[test]
   330	fn collab_session_attach_websocket_round_trip_via_echo() {
   331	    // Highest-value test: wire WebSocketTransport into CollabSession
   332	    // under OnAppend; verify the V2 V3 step 2 + step 3 contract
   333	    // (auto-flush + offline-write reattach) holds over a REAL
   334	    // WebSocket, not just LoopbackTransport.
   335	    let rt = runtime();
   336	    rt.block_on(async {
   337	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   338	        let ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   339	            .await
   340	            .expect("handshake");
   341	
   342	        let mut session = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1)).expect("session");
   343	        session.attach_transport(ws);
   344	        session.set_auto_flush_policy(AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend);
   345	
   346	        // OnAppend + attached WS: each append flushes the delta over
   347	        // the wire. The echo server reflects each blob back; the
   348	        // session's poll_remote drains the inbox and merges.
   349	        session.append_op(add_sheet()).expect("add_sheet");
   350	        session.append_op(put_value(0, 0, 0, 42.0)).expect("put");
   351	
   352	        // Poll until we've drained the echoes (auto-flush is one
   353	        // direction; the echo server reflects each blob back as a
   354	        // separate frame). Loro dedupes on import — but the import
   355	        // still returns the blob count, NOT op count.
   356	        let mut total_merged = 0usize;
   357	        for _ in 0..50 {
   358	            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
   359	            let merged = session.poll_remote().expect("poll");
   360	            total_merged += merged;
   361	            if total_merged >= 2 {
   362	                break;
   363	            }
   364	        }
   365	        assert!(
   366	            total_merged >= 1,
   367	            "session.poll_remote MUST receive at least one echoed blob, got {total_merged}"
   368	        );
   369	
   370	        // Session op_count = 2 (add_sheet + put_value). Echo didn't
   371	        // change it (Loro dedupes own peer's ops on re-import).
   372	        assert_eq!(session.op_count(), 2, "Loro dedup keeps op_count stable");
   373	
   374	        // has_pending_flush should be false after auto-flush
   375	        // completed (V2 V3 step 1 idempotency guard).
   376	        assert!(
   377	            !session.has_pending_flush(),
   378	            "OnAppend + attached WS leaves session synced post-mutator"
   379	        );
   380	    });
   381	}

   383	#[test]
   384	fn collab_session_websocket_reattach_after_close_delivers_offline_ops() {
   385	    // V2 V3 step 3 contract: append while transport detached; reattach
   386	    // (or attach new transport); next auto-flush delivers all
   387	    // accumulated ops. Verifies the contract holds for WS transport
   388	    // identically to LoopbackTransport.
   389	    let rt = runtime();
   390	    rt.block_on(async {
   391	        let mut session = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1)).expect("session");
   392	        session.set_auto_flush_policy(AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend);
   393	
   394	        // Phase 1: NO transport attached. Append ops — they commit
   395	        // locally; maybe_auto_flush no-ops.
   396	        session.append_op(add_sheet()).expect("add_sheet offline");
   397	        session
   398	            .append_op(put_value(0, 0, 0, 1.0))
   399	            .expect("put offline");
   400	        session
   401	            .append_op(put_value(0, 0, 1, 2.0))
   402	            .expect("put offline");
   403	        assert!(session.has_pending_flush(), "offline ops are pending");
   404	        assert!(!session.has_transport());
   405	
   406	        // Phase 2: attach WS. attach_transport resets
   407	        // last_flushed_vv = None per V2 V3 step 1 contract.
   408	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   409	        let ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   410	            .await
   411	            .expect("handshake");
   412	        session.attach_transport(ws);
   413	        assert!(session.has_transport());
   414	        // attach_transport itself doesn't auto-flush (V2 V2 design).
   415	        // The next mutator OR explicit flush_delta_to_transport
   416	        // delivers all accumulated ops.
   417	
   418	        // Phase 3: explicit flush sends from empty VV → all 3 ops
   419	        // delivered as a single delta blob to the server, which
   420	        // echoes it back. Session's poll_remote then drains the
   421	        // echoed blob; Loro dedupes own ops.
   422	        session
   423	            .flush_delta_to_transport()
   424	            .expect("explicit flush succeeds");
   425	        assert!(
   426	            !session.has_pending_flush(),
   427	            "flush leaves session synced (current_vv == last_flushed_vv)"
   428	        );
   429	
   430	        // Drain echo.
   431	        let mut total_merged = 0usize;
   432	        for _ in 0..50 {
   433	            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
   434	            total_merged += session.poll_remote().expect("poll");
   435	            if total_merged >= 1 {
   436	                break;
   437	            }
   438	        }
   439	        assert!(
   440	            total_merged >= 1,
   441	            "post-reattach flush blob MUST be echoed back, got {total_merged}"
   442	        );
   443	        assert_eq!(
   444	            session.op_count(),
   445	            3,
   446	            "3 offline ops preserved through reattach"
   447	        );
   448	    });
   449	}

   488	#[test]
   489	fn last_error_populated_after_peer_disconnect() {
   490	    let rt = runtime();
   491	    rt.block_on(async {
   492	        // V2 V3 step 4 audit closure (Opus M1): pin the contract that
   493	        // the reader task stashes a RuntimeError when it observes a
   494	        // peer disconnect (non-graceful TCP teardown).
   495	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   496	        let mut ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   497	            .await
   498	            .expect("handshake");
   499	
   500	        // Drop server: per-conn task aborted → TCP socket dropped →
   501	        // reader observes EOF or Err on next stream poll.
   502	        drop(server);
   503	
   504	        // Loop try_recv until Closed observed, then check last_error.
   505	        let mut closed_seen = false;
   506	        for _ in 0..50 {
   507	            match ws.try_recv() {
   508	                Ok(None) => tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await,
   509	                Ok(Some(_)) => continue,
   510	                Err(TransportError::Closed) => {
   511	                    closed_seen = true;
   512	                    break;
   513	                }
   514	                Err(other) => panic!("unexpected error: {other:?}"),
   515	            }
   516	        }
   517	        assert!(closed_seen, "Closed must be observed after peer disconnect");
   518	
   519	        // The peer disconnect may surface either as a graceful EOF
   520	        // (None on stream → leaves last_error None) or as an Err on
   520	        // (None on stream → leaves last_error None) or as an Err on
   521	        // the next poll (populates RuntimeError). Both are valid task
   522	        // exit paths under TCP teardown; the contract is "Some when
   523	        // an Err arm fired, None when a clean None arm fired." Don't
   524	        // overpin which one this specific platform exhibits — pin
   525	        // only that the accessor returns SOMETHING readable without
   526	        // panicking, and if Some, it's a RuntimeError.
   527	        if let Some(err) = ws.last_error() {
   528	            assert!(
   529	                matches!(err, WebSocketError::RuntimeError(_)),
   530	                "last_error after disconnect must be RuntimeError variant if present, got {err:?}"
   531	            );
   532	        }
   533	    });
   534	}

   537	fn peer_disconnect_always_populates_last_error_step_5_closure() {
   538	    // **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Codex L2 + Opus-B M4):** the
   539	    // prior step-4 behavior left last_error=None for both clean
   540	    // caller-close AND for stream-end-None (peer dropped TCP without
   541	    // a Close frame). Closure: stream-end now populates a sentinel
   542	    // RuntimeError("peer stream ended without close frame") so
   543	    // callers can distinguish. (Clean caller-close still leaves
   544	    // last_error=None per the contract.)
   545	    let rt = runtime();
   546	    rt.block_on(async {
   547	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   548	        let mut ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   549	            .await
   550	            .expect("handshake");
   551	
   552	        drop(server);
   553	
   554	        // Wait for reader to observe disconnect.
   555	        for _ in 0..50 {
   556	            match ws.try_recv() {
   557	                Ok(None) => tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await,
   558	                Ok(Some(_)) => continue,
   559	                Err(TransportError::Closed) => break,
   560	                Err(other) => panic!("unexpected error: {other:?}"),
   561	            }
   562	        }
   563	
   564	        let err = ws.last_error();
   565	        assert!(
   566	            err.is_some(),
   567	            "peer disconnect MUST populate last_error post-step-5 (was previously possibly None)"
   568	        );
   569	        let msg = format!("{err:?}");
   570	        // The message should hint at either an Err arm (tungstenite
   571	        // string) or the new stream-end sentinel.
   572	        assert!(
   573	            msg.contains("RuntimeError"),
   574	            "last_error must be RuntimeError variant, got {msg}"
   575	        );
   576	    });

   585	    // **V2 V3 step 5 megaudit closure (Opus-A H1):** pin the

   587	    // through to `WebSocketTransport::last_error()` after the

   648	#[test]
   649	fn flush_pending_with_no_pending_returns_ok_immediately() {
   650	    // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** baseline — flush_pending on a
   651	    // freshly-connected transport with nothing queued returns Ok
   652	    // without blocking.
   653	    //
   654	    // Uses multi_thread_runtime because flush_pending is a blocking-
   655	    // sync call that would deadlock on a single-threaded runtime
   656	    // (writer task can't make progress while the worker is blocked).
   657	    // See the helper docstring + Transport::flush_pending async-
   658	    // context caveat.
   659	    let rt = multi_thread_runtime();

   664	            .expect("handshake");

   666	        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
   667	        let result = ws.flush_pending();
   668	        let elapsed = start.elapsed();
   669	
   670	        assert!(
   671	            result.is_ok(),
   672	            "flush_pending with no pending bytes MUST return Ok"
   673	        );
   674	        assert!(
   675	            elapsed < Duration::from_millis(50),
   676	            "flush_pending with no pending bytes MUST not block (took {elapsed:?})"
   677	        );

   681	#[test]
   682	fn flush_pending_blocks_until_writer_catches_up() {
   683	    // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** pin the blocking-then-Ok semantic.
   684	    // Send several blobs; immediately call flush_pending. Verify it
   685	    // returns Ok AFTER the writer task has caught up (i.e., the echo
   686	    // server has reflected the blobs back).
   687	    let rt = multi_thread_runtime();
   688	    rt.block_on(async {
   689	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   690	        let mut ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   691	            .await
   692	            .expect("handshake");
   693	
   694	        for i in 0..5u8 {
   695	            ws.send(&[i, i + 1, i + 2]).expect("send");
   696	        }
   697	
   698	        // flush_pending should block until all 5 sends are flushed.
   699	        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
   700	        let result = ws.flush_pending();
   701	        let elapsed = start.elapsed();
   702	
   703	        assert!(
   704	            result.is_ok(),
   705	            "flush_pending after 5 sends MUST return Ok once writer drains, got {result:?}"
   706	        );
   707	        // Some blocking time is expected (mpsc + ws_sink + tokio
   708	        // scheduling). Upper bound is generous for slow CI.
   709	        assert!(
   710	            elapsed < Duration::from_secs(2),
   711	            "flush_pending blocked unreasonably long: {elapsed:?}"
   712	        );
   713	
   714	        // Echo verification: each blob should have been sent over
   715	        // the wire (and echoed back).
   716	        let mut received = 0;
   717	        for _ in 0..30 {
   718	            match ws.try_recv() {
   719	                Ok(Some(_)) => received += 1,
   720	                Ok(None) => tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await,
   721	                Err(_) => break,
   722	            }
   723	            if received >= 5 {
   724	                break;
   725	            }
   726	        }
   727	        assert_eq!(
   728	            received, 5,
   729	            "all 5 blobs MUST have been flushed (and echoed back), got {received}"
   730	        );
   731	    });
   732	}

   734	#[test]
   735	fn flush_pending_after_close_returns_closed() {
   736	    // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** closed-state fast-path. If the
   737	    // transport is already closed on entry, flush_pending returns
   738	    // Err(Closed) immediately — regardless of whether the local
   739	    // progress counter has caught up.
   740	    //
   741	    // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 audit closure (Codex M1, 2026-05-21):** prior
   742	    // version of this test accepted EITHER Ok OR Err(Closed) because
   743	    // the impl returned Ok if `counter >= target` on entry, even when
   744	    // closed. The audit caught the docstring-vs-impl divergence. The
   745	    // closure inverted the impl to check `closed` BEFORE the
   746	    // counter-vs-target check, so closed-on-entry now uniformly
   747	    // returns Err(Closed) per the documented contract.
   748	    let rt = multi_thread_runtime();
   749	    rt.block_on(async {
   750	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   751	        let mut ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   752	            .await
   753	            .expect("handshake");
   754	
   755	        // Queue a few sends, close the transport explicitly, then
   756	        // flush_pending.
   757	        ws.send(b"a").expect("send");
   758	        ws.send(b"b").expect("send");
   759	        ws.close();
   760	
   761	        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
   762	        let result = ws.flush_pending();
   763	        let elapsed = start.elapsed();
   764	
   765	        assert!(
   766	            matches!(result, Err(TransportError::Closed)),
   767	            "flush_pending after explicit close MUST return Err(Closed), got {result:?}"
   768	        );
   769	        assert!(
   770	            elapsed < Duration::from_millis(50),
   771	            "closed-on-entry flush_pending MUST be near-instant (skip the wait loop), got {elapsed:?}"
   772	        );
   773	    });
   774	}

   776	#[test]
   777	fn flush_pending_returns_closed_if_server_drops_mid_flush() {
   778	    // **V2 V4 V1 step 1 (Tier K1):** pin the "writer fails mid-flush"
   779	    // path. Server is dropped while flush_pending is parked on the
   780	    // Condvar. Reader task sees disconnect → sets closed → notifies
   781	    // Condvar (via Drop on EchoServer aborting per-conn tasks → TCP
   782	    // socket dies → ws_stream errors → reader sets closed). The
   783	    // writer task notify_all on closed-flag transition wakes up
   784	    // flush_pending which observes the closed flag and returns
   785	    // Err(Closed).
   786	    let rt = multi_thread_runtime();
   787	    rt.block_on(async {
   788	        let server = EchoServer::start().await;
   789	        let mut ws = WebSocketTransport::connect(&server.url())
   790	            .await
   791	            .expect("handshake");
   792	
   793	        // Queue some sends.
   794	        ws.send(b"in-flight-1").expect("send");
   795	        ws.send(b"in-flight-2").expect("send");
   796	
   797	        // Drop the server — TCP socket dies on per-conn abort.
   798	        drop(server);
   799	
   800	        // flush_pending should eventually observe the closed state and
   801	        // return Err. Acceptable: also returns Ok if the writer
   802	        // happened to send both blobs before the TCP teardown was
   803	        // observed.
   804	        let start = std::time::Instant::now();
   805	        let result = ws.flush_pending();
   806	        let elapsed = start.elapsed();
   807

**VERDICT**: PASS-WITH-FINDINGS  
Strongest concern: the core V8-block fix is sound, but the V2.6 fixture/test plan needs changes because `new BlockingTransport(...)` is not attachable through the current NAPI surface and the proposed timing test can still pass vacuously.

**Findings**

**M - Capture the drain target in the handle, not inside `wait_for_drain`.**  
Current `WebSocketTransport::send` increments `queued_count` after enqueue ([crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:657](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:657), [lib.rs:664](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:664)), and current `flush_pending` snapshots the target at call time ([lib.rs:745](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:745)). If the V2.5 handle loads `queued_count` later inside the blocking task, it can include sends queued after the JS call released the session lock. This does not reopen V8-block, but it drifts from the documented “previously queued” contract ([crates/ql-collab/src/transport.rs:201](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/transport.rs:201)).  
Recommendation: store `target: u64` in `WebSocketProgressAckHandle`, captured in `ack_handle()` before returning.

**M - The BlockingTransport JS shape needs redesign.**  
`attachTransport` currently accepts only the native `Transport` wrapper ([crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:480](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:480)), whose actual payload is `Option<Box<dyn CoreTransport + Send>>` ([lib.rs:919](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:919), [lib.rs:924](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:924)). A separate `new engine.BlockingTransport(...)` class will not be attachable unless the plan adds an adapter.  
Recommendation: expose a test fixture controller with `takeTransport(): Transport`, `release()`, and preferably `waitUntilBlocked(): Promise<void>`.

**M - The contract test needs a deterministic “wait entered” signal.**  
The existing V2.4 tests already document that Loopback makes the interleaving tests vacuous ([quantbook-roundtrip.test.ts:1211](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab/extensions/quantlab/test/quantbook-roundtrip.test.ts:1211), [quantbook-roundtrip.test.ts:1235](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab/extensions/quantlab/test/quantbook-roundtrip.test.ts:1235)). The proposed immediate `opCount()` can still run before `flushPendingToTransport` has reached the blocking wait.  
Recommendation: wait for the fixture to report “blocked”, then measure `opCount`. Use a relative assertion such as `elapsed < blockMs / 2`, with `blockMs >= 1000`, rather than a fixed 100 ms threshold.

**M - Do not change `Transport` to `pub trait Transport: Send`.**  
Current `Transport` has no supertrait ([crates/ql-collab/src/transport.rs:128](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/transport.rs:128)); attach paths already require `Send` where needed ([crates/ql-collab/src/session.rs:342](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/session.rs:342), [session.rs:726](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/session.rs:726)). Adding a `Send` supertrait is not “non-breaking” for external custom transports.  
Recommendation: keep `pub trait Transport`; add only the default `ack_handle(&self)` method.

**L - Re-export `FlushAck`.**  
The binding plan uses `ql_collab::FlushAck`, but current public re-export only includes `LoopbackTransport`, `NoopTransport`, `Transport`, and `TransportError` ([crates/ql-collab/src/lib.rs:111](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/lib.rs:111)). Add `FlushAck` there.

**Q1: Verified, with the target-snapshot fix above.**  
The V2.4 bug is real: the current binding locks the session inside `spawn_blocking` and calls `guard.flush_pending_to_transport()` while holding it ([crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:831](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:831), [lib.rs:835](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:835)). A scoped guard is dropped at the closing brace; `MutexGuard::drop` unlocks the mutex ([lock_api mutex.rs:701](/Users/sanzhar/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/lock_api-0.4.14/src/mutex.rs:701)). The proposed handle can wait without the session mutex because the websocket progress state is already in `Arc`s ([crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:301](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:301), [lib.rs:315](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:315)), and the writer task updates that state directly ([lib.rs:412](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:412), [lib.rs:440](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:440)).

**Q2: Box design is acceptable.**  
`Box<dyn FlushAck + Send>` is the right shape for a per-call target snapshot. `Arc<dyn FlushAck>` is less useful if the handle should not be reused across flush calls. `async-trait` is unnecessary because the current trait is explicitly blocking-sync ([crates/ql-collab/src/transport.rs:231](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/transport.rs:231)). Option C remains worse because it changes sync method behavior/API ([docs/audits/2026-05-22-phase-5-7-v2-4-opus.md:267](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-22-phase-5-7-v2-4-opus.md:267)). Notify-only does not solve the hazard unless the session lock is also released; the current session proxy is still `&mut self` + sync wait ([crates/ql-collab/src/session.rs:855](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/session.rs:855)).

**Q3: Needs change.**  
Use deterministic synchronization plus a relative timing assertion. A plain 500 ms block with `elapsed < 100` is vulnerable to scheduler jitter and to the “flush task not yet blocking” race. Existing mocha timeout is 10s ([package.json:20](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab/extensions/quantlab/package.json:20)), so a 1000 ms fixture with `elapsed < blockMs / 2` is still cheap.

**Q4: Feature-gate or keep binding-local test-only.**  
Recommendation: do not ship `BlockingTransport` as production API. Prefer a `test-fixtures` feature, or define the fixture privately in `ql-bindings-node` under that feature if only mocha needs it. Current build docs use plain `cargo build -p ql-bindings-node --release` ([quantbook-roundtrip.test.ts:19](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab/extensions/quantlab/test/quantbook-roundtrip.test.ts:19)), so the plan must update CI/test build commands to enable the feature.

**Risks 5-9**

5. **Detach mid-wait: L.** Drop sets `closed = true`, notifies, then aborts tasks ([crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:633](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:633)). Worst-case lost wake waits for the 100 ms timeout ([lib.rs:754](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:754)). Acceptable.

6. **Box allocation overhead: L.** One allocation per `flushPendingToTransport`; dominated by `spawn_blocking` submission already used today ([crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:834](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-bindings-node/src/lib.rs:834)).

7. **Arc cloning soundness: L.** The cloned websocket state remains alive after transport drop via `Arc` fields ([crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:292](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:292), [lib.rs:315](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab-ws/src/lib.rs:315)). No UAF; closed flag terminates the wait.

8. **Existing tests: L if trait stays non-supertrait; M if `Transport: Send` is added.** The default method is additive, but a `Send` supertrait changes the public implementor contract. Internal custom transports appear Send, but this still needs compile verification after implementation.

9. **`FlushAck: Send` vs `Send + Sync`: L.** `Send` is sufficient because the boxed handle is moved into one blocking task. Add `Sync` only if you switch to `Arc<dyn FlushAck>` or shared handles.

Final verdict remains **PASS-WITH-FINDINGS**: the V2.5 engine refactor direction is sound; fix the target snapshot and V2.6 fixture/test shape before shipping.
